definition_zh: 通信系统；信息从发送者传到接收者的一整套通道与规则；（引申）一个社会或组织维持联络的整体安排
definition_en: the whole set of channels, codes and rules by which messages travel from a sender to a receiver
core_image: 深谷两侧各立一座铁塔，话音被拆成电码沿铁塔与光缆传过去，到对岸再拼回人声
scene: 山两侧的村落隔着深谷，人们把话交给铁塔与光缆，话音在对岸重新拼回原声。The communication system carried a greeting across the valley faster than a runner could walk it.
sceneCN: 这里 communication system 指信息从发送者传到接收者的一整套通道与规则（第 1 个义项：作为整体安排）；句意为这套通信系统把一句问候送过山谷，比人跑过去还快。

pos.zh: 通信系统；信息传递体系（可数，指一套通道与规则）
（生物学）动物的信号传递系统（可数）

derivatives.zh: 交流；传递（由拉丁 communicare 直接借入，核心是「使信息成为共同所有」，侧重动作）
交流；通信（由基础动词加表过程或结果的名词后缀而来，由动作转指过程与内容，是本词组的基础名词）
乐于交流的；传达性的（由基础动词加表性质的形容词后缀而来，由动作转指性质）
传讯者；善于表达的人（由基础动词加表施事者的名词后缀而来，由动作转指施事的人）
系统性的；全身的（由基础名词加表属性的形容词后缀而来，由「整体」转指「属于整体结构」）

senses.title: The whole arrangement
senses.definition: the complete set of channels, codes and rules that lets messages pass from sender to receiver
senses.definitionCN: 让信息从发送者抵达接收者的全部通道、编码与规则
senses.example: A reliable communication system is the first need of any remote field station.
senses.exampleCN: 对任何偏远野外观测站来说，一套可靠的通信系统是首要需求。
senses.why: The two words name a circuit, not a device: system supplies the idea of parts standing together as one working whole.
senses.whyCN: 这两个词命名的是一条回路，而不是一台设备：后一个词提供「多个部分合成一个运作整体」的意思。

senses.title: The hardware network
senses.definition: the physical infrastructure of cables, towers, satellites and switches that carries signals
senses.definitionCN: 由电缆、铁塔、卫星与交换机等实体设施构成的信号承载网络
senses.example: The storm disabled the region's communication system for two days.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴让该地区的通信系统瘫痪了两天。
senses.why: Once messages travel by wire, the arrangement becomes visible as hardware, and the word shifts from rules to machinery.
senses.whyCN: 一旦信息靠线路传输，这套安排就以硬件的形式显形，词义也从规则转向机器。

senses.title: Signalling in the body
senses.definition: the ways animals exchange information by sound, scent, gesture or dance
senses.definitionCN: 动物用声音、气味、姿态或舞蹈交换信息的方式
senses.example: Bees rely on a chemical communication system inside the hive.
senses.exampleCN: 蜜蜂在蜂巢内依靠一套化学通信系统。
senses.why: The same circuit exists without any technology: a sender, a signal, a channel and a receiver can all be organic.
senses.whyCN: 同一条回路不需要技术也能存在：发送者、信号、通道与接收者都可以是生物体。

senses.title: A society's media order
senses.definition: the mix of speech, print and broadcast through which a whole population shares news
senses.definitionCN: 一个全体人口借以共享消息的言谈、印刷与广播的组合
senses.example: Print created a national communication system out of scattered local dialects.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷把零散的地方方言编织成一套全国性的通信体系。
senses.why: A society also sends messages to itself; its media form a system with its own reach, speed and blind spots.
senses.whyCN: 社会也在给自己发消息；它的媒介构成一个有特定覆盖、速度与盲区的系统。

senses.title: Information flow in an organization
senses.definition: the fixed routes and routines by which orders, reports and records move inside a body
senses.definitionCN: 命令、报告与档案在一个机构内部流动的固定路线与惯例
senses.example: The army rebuilt its communication system after the radio failure.
senses.exampleCN: 无线电故障之后，部队重建了它的通信体系。
senses.why: An organization is held together by messages going up and down; the routes themselves are what the phrase names here.
senses.whyCN: 组织靠上下流动的消息维持一体；这里命名的正是那些路线本身。

senses.title: A shared protocol
senses.definition: a standard format and set of rules that two devices must follow to exchange data
senses.definitionCN: 两台设备交换数据时必须遵循的标准格式与规则
senses.example: The two devices share a common communication system, so they pair at once.
senses.exampleCN: 两台设备共用一套通信协议，所以立刻就能配对。
senses.why: Compatibility is a code agreement; the smallest system two machines can share is one common way of formatting a signal.
senses.whyCN: 兼容性就是一种编码约定；两台机器能共用的最小系统，就是一套共同的信号格式。

senses.title: One person's means of contact
senses.definition: the informal set of tools a person uses to stay in touch with others
senses.definitionCN: 一个人用来与他人保持联系的非正式工具组合
senses.example: Her only communication system is a phone and two messaging apps.
senses.exampleCN: 她唯一的联络手段是一部手机和两个聊天软件。
senses.why: Everyday use shrinks the system to whatever sits in one pocket: the word stretches from institutions down to a personal kit.
senses.whyCN: 日常用法把系统缩小到口袋里那点东西：词义从制度一路延伸到个人的工具包。

senses.title: The model in communication theory
senses.definition: a formal model of sender, message, channel, noise and receiver used to measure information
senses.definitionCN: 由发送者、消息、通道、噪声与接收者构成、用于度量信息的正式模型
senses.example: Shannon modelled the communication system as a sender, a channel and a receiver.
senses.exampleCN: 香农把通信系统建模为发送者、通道与接收者。
senses.why: Theory strips away people and wires and keeps only the boxes and arrows, turning the phrase into an abstract object of study.
senses.whyCN: 理论剥去人与线路，只留下方框与箭头，于是这个词组变成了抽象的研究对象。

intro.en: The phrase joins communication, from Latin communicatio 'a making common', and system, from Greek systema 'a whole compounded of parts'. It became a technical term with telegraphy and was formalized in information theory. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词组由 communication（来自拉丁 communicatio「使共同」）与 system（来自希腊 systema「由多部分合成的整体」）组合而成。它随电报技术成为术语，又在信息论中被形式化。年代均为约数。

items.en: Communicare 'to share, impart' comes from communis 'common, shared'. The usual analysis is com- 'together' plus munus 'duty, gift, office'; the deeper origin of munus is not established.
items.cn: communicare「分享、传达」来自 communis「共同的、共享的」。通行分析是前缀表「共同」加 munus「职责、赠礼、公务」；munus 更深的来源未得到证明。

items.en: Communicatio was the noun of action for 'a making common, an imparting', already used for sharing speech and goods.
items.cn: communicatio 是表示「使共同、传达」的动作名词，早已用于分享言谈与财物。

items.en: Systema meant 'an organized body, a whole of several parts', built on syn- 'together' and histanai 'to cause to stand'.
items.cn: systema 意为「有组织的整体、由若干部分合成的整体」，由表示「一起」的成分与 histanai「使站立」构成。

items.en: Late Latin borrowed systema as 'a whole, an organized body'; English system followed through French in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语借入 systema，义为「整体、有组织的身体」；英语 system 在十六世纪经法语进入。

items.en: In the nineteenth century communication system became a practical term for the wires, stations and codes that carried messages over distance.
items.cn: 十九世纪，communication system 成为实用术语，指远距离传递消息的线路、站点与电码。

items.en: Shannon's 1948 model fixed the modern technical reading: a source, a transmitter, a channel with noise, and a receiver. The phrase was thereby turned into a measurable object.
items.cn: 香农在一九四八年的模型确定了现代技术读法：信源、发送器、带噪声的通道与接收者。这个词组由此变成可度量的对象。

note.en: Group one contains words built from the same two roots; group two holds near neighbours for networks and information flow.
note.cn: 第一组是由同样两个词根构成的词；第二组是网络与信息流方面的近邻词。

entries.definition: The act or process of exchanging information; it lacks the system's emphasis on connected parts.
entries.definitionCN: 交换信息的动作或过程；它没有 system 那种「各部分连成整体」的重点。

entries.definition: A group of people sharing something; it comes from the same 'common' root but names people, not channels.
entries.definitionCN: 共享某物的一群人；同出「共同」词根，却指人，不指通道。

entries.definition: Shared participation, often religious; it names the sharing itself, not a technical network.
entries.definitionCN: 共同的参与，常用于宗教；它指共享本身，而非技术网络。

entries.definition: Any set of connected parts; alone it says nothing about messages or signals.
entries.definitionCN: 任何由相连部分构成的整体；单用时与消息或信号无关。

entries.definition: The linked nodes themselves; a communication system adds the codes and rules that make the links carry meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 相互连接的节点本身；通信系统还要加上使连接能承载意义的编码与规则。

entries.definition: The physical facilities a society needs; it is broader and says nothing about messages.
entries.definitionCN: 社会所需的实体设施；范围更宽，且不涉及消息。

entries.definition: A system of signals, common for railways and cells; it stresses the signs rather than the whole organisation.
entries.definitionCN: 信号构成的系统，常用于铁路与细胞；它强调信号本身，而非整个组织。

entries.definition: A system for storing and processing data; it foregrounds records and computation rather than transmission.
entries.definitionCN: 用于存储与处理数据的系统；它突出记录与计算，而非传输。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real technical phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的复合词与真实的技术说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Communication carries 'common': a message becomes common property once it arrives.
normal.cn: communication 含着「共同」：消息一到，就成了双方共同拥有的东西。

normal.en: System means parts standing together, so the phrase is literally 'the standing-together of shared messages'.
normal.cn: system 意为各部分站在一起，所以这个词组字面上就是「共享消息的一体化」。

normal.en: The telegraph gave the phrase its modern body: wires, stations and codes.
normal.cn: 电报给了这个词组现代的身体：线路、站点与电码。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale: a modern communication system, the global communication system, communication system design.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出尺度：现代通信系统、全球通信系统、通信系统设计。

normal.en: The plural communication systems and the unchanged attributive form are both standard.
normal.cn: 复数 communication systems 与作定语时不变形，都是标准用法。

abstract.en: Picture two towers facing each other across a valley, each one repeating what it hears.
abstract.cn: 想象两座塔隔着山谷相对，各自把听到的东西复述出去。

abstract.en: Picture the body as a network of nerves where a signal is never stored, only passed on.
abstract.cn: 想象身体是一张神经网络，信号从不被储存，只被传递。

abstract.en: Picture a society as a single ear listening to its own broadcast, deciding what counts as news.
abstract.cn: 想象一个社会是一只耳朵，听着自己的广播，并决定什么才算新闻。

examples.en: Engineers extended the communication system to the last village in the valley.
examples.cn: 工程师把通信系统延伸到了山谷里最后一个村庄。

examples.en: Ants use a chemical communication system that no satellite can intercept.
examples.cn: 蚂蚁使用一套化学通信系统，任何卫星都无法截获。

examples.en: A company's communication system fails when bad news travels slower than good news.
examples.cn: 当一个公司的坏消息比好消息传得慢，它的通信体系就失灵了。

dict_mnemonic.text: communication（使共同）+ system（各部分站在一起）＝ 让消息在各方之间成为共同财产的那套安排；记「有发有收，中间有路」。

root: communication 源自拉丁 communicare「使共同、传达」，其词根 communis 意为「共同的」，一般分析为前缀表「共同」加 mūnus「职责、赠礼」，mūnus 更深的来源不确定；system 源自希腊 systema「由多部分合成的整体」，由前缀表「一起」加 histanai「使站立」构成，更早形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one circuit at different scales: the whole arrangement, its hardware, a body's signals, a society's media, an organisation's routes, a shared protocol, one person's kit, and the theorist's model.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一回路在不同尺度上的取景：整体安排、硬件网络、生物信号、社会媒介、组织路线、共用协议、个人工具，以及理论家的模型。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a message leaves one mouth, passes through towers and codes, and arrives whole at another ear.
core.cn: 核心意象：消息离开一张嘴，穿过铁塔与编码，完整地抵达另一只耳朵。

branches.en: ARRANGEMENT AND HARDWARE: first the whole set of rules, then the metal and glass that carry them.
branches.cn: 安排与硬件：先是整套规则，再是承载规则的金属与玻璃。

branches.en: THE BODY AS NETWORK: animals run the same circuit with scent and dance instead of wire.
branches.cn: 身体即网络：动物用气味与舞蹈代替线路，跑着同一条回路。

branches.en: SOCIETY AND ORGANISATION: a population and a staff each need routes for news and orders.
branches.cn: 社会与组织：一个全体人口与一个工作班子，都需要消息与命令的路线。

branches.en: PROTOCOL AND POCKET: compatibility between machines, then the few tools one person carries.
branches.cn: 协议与口袋：机器之间的兼容，然后再缩小到一个人随身带的几件工具。

branches.en: THE THEORIST'S BOXES: people and wires drop out, leaving sender, channel and receiver.
branches.cn: 理论家的方框：人与线路退场，只剩发送者、通道与接收者。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two borrowings whose parts still recur in English: a Latin root for 'common' and a Greek root for 'standing together'.
intro.cn: 这个词组由两个借词构成，它们的构件在英语中仍然反复出现：一个拉丁词根表示「共同」，一个希腊词根表示「站在一起」。

latinIntro.en: Latin communis and communicare supply the first half; Greek systema, borrowed into Late Latin, supplies the second. The two families never merged in Latin, so the English phrase is a modern assembly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 communis 与 communicare 提供前半部分；借入晚期拉丁语的希腊 systema 提供后半部分。这两个词族在拉丁语中从未合并，因此英语这个词组是现代的拼装。

items.meaning: to share information, thoughts or feelings
items.meaningCN: 交流；传达（信息、想法或感受）
items.example: They communicate by radio every morning.
items.exampleCN: 他们每天早上用无线电联络。

items.meaning: the process or content of exchanging messages
items.meaningCN: 交流；通信（交换消息的过程或内容）
items.example: Clear communication prevents most delays.
items.exampleCN: 清晰的沟通能避免大多数延误。

items.example: She is unusually communicative about her work.
items.exampleCN: 她对自己的工作异常乐于交流。

items.meaning: a person skilled at conveying messages
items.example: A good communicator repeats the main point.
items.exampleCN: 善于表达的人会重复要点。

items.meaning: able to be passed on, often of disease
items.meaningCN: 可传达的；（疾病）可传染的
items.example: The infection is highly communicable.
items.exampleCN: 这种感染传染性很强。

items.meaning: a set of connected parts working as one
items.meaningCN: 系统；由相连部分构成的整体
items.example: The heating system failed in winter.
items.exampleCN: 供暖系统在冬天坏了。

items.meaning: affecting the whole body or structure
items.example: The problem is systemic, not local.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题是系统性的，不是局部的。

items.meaning: done according to an ordered plan
items.example: They made a systematic search of the archive.
items.exampleCN: 他们对档案做了系统性的查找。

items.meaning: to arrange into an ordered whole
items.meaningCN: 使系统化；把……整理成体系
items.example: She systematized the office records.
items.exampleCN: 她把办公室的档案系统化了。

items.meaning: the act of arranging into a system
items.meaningCN: 系统化（把零散事物整理成体系的过程）
items.example: The systematization of the data took a year.
items.exampleCN: 把这些数据系统化花了一年。

latinEntries.structure: systema (n., Greek, borrowed into Late Latin)
latinEntries.meaning: an organized whole of several parts
latinEntries.meaningCN: 由若干部分构成的有组织整体

definition_zh: 口头传统；以口耳相传代代延续的故事、歌谣与知识；口述史研究中的口头资料体系
definition_en: the body of stories, songs and knowledge that a community passes on by speech rather than by writing
core_image: 火堆旁，老人开口讲起，孩子跟着复述，同一段故事在每一代人嘴里略微改变
scene: 火堆旁，老人把祖辈的故事讲给围坐的孩子，孩子第二天又学着讲给更小的孩子听。An oral tradition kept the story alive without a single written page.
sceneCN: 这里 oral tradition 指以口耳相传延续的故事与知识（第 1 个义项：作为整体传统）；句意为口头传统让这个故事一页纸都没写也活了下来。

pos.zh: 口头传统（可数，指某一群体的传统；不可数，指这种传承方式）

derivatives.zh: 口头地（由基础形容词加表方式的副词后缀而来，由形容词转指方式）
传统的（由基础名词加表属性的形容词后缀而来，由名词转指性质）
传统主义（由基础形容词加表主张的名词后缀而来，由性质转指主张）
传统主义者（由基础形容词加表主张者的名词后缀而来，由主张转指持主张的人）

senses.title: The transmitted body
senses.definition: the whole body of stories, songs, laws and knowledge a community hands on by speech
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体靠言谈代代传下的故事、歌谣、规矩与知识的总和
senses.example: The village's oral tradition includes songs that no book records.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子的口头传统里有任何书都没有记录的歌。
senses.why: Tradition is what is handed over; oral fixes the medium. Together they name a body of material, not a single telling.
senses.whyCN: 前者指被递交下来的东西，后者限定媒介；合起来命名的是一批材料，而非某一次讲述。

senses.title: The medium itself
senses.definition: transmission through voice and memory instead of writing
senses.definitionCN: 依靠嗓音与记忆而不是文字来传递的方式
senses.example: The epic survived for centuries through oral tradition alone.
senses.exampleCN: 这部史诗仅靠口头传统就流传了几个世纪。
senses.why: Here the phrase names the channel rather than the content: speech, memory and repetition do the work of a book.
senses.whyCN: 这里命名的不是内容而是通道：言谈、记忆与复述承担了书本的工作。

senses.title: A family's or clan's account
senses.definition: the particular version of events that one lineage recites about its own past
senses.definitionCN: 某一世系关于自身过去的特定讲述版本
senses.example: His family's oral tradition places the first ancestor in the northern hills.
senses.exampleCN: 他家口头传下的说法把最早的祖先放在北边的山里。
senses.why: Every group keeps its own version; the phrase can narrow from a whole culture to one family's handed-down account.
senses.whyCN: 每个群体都保留自己的版本；这个词组可以从整个文化收窄到一户人家的口传说法。

senses.title: Oral history as method
senses.definition: recorded interviews and testimony used by historians as evidence
senses.definitionCN: 历史学者用作证据的录音访谈与证言
senses.example: Her research combines oral tradition with colonial tax records.
senses.exampleCN: 她的研究把口述材料与殖民时期的税册结合起来。
senses.why: Once a tape recorder is added, spoken memory becomes an archive; the phrase then names a research method.
senses.whyCN: 一旦加上录音机，口传记忆就变成档案；这个词组于是命名一种研究方法。

senses.title: Customary law recited
senses.definition: rules that are remembered and spoken aloud rather than written in a code
senses.definitionCN: 靠记忆与当众诵说、而非写成法典的规则
senses.example: The elders settled the dispute according to oral tradition.
senses.exampleCN: 长老们依照口传的习惯法解决了这场纠纷。
senses.why: Law can live in trained memory; where no code exists, the same phrase covers the binding rules of the community.
senses.whyCN: 法律可以活在受过训练的记忆里；在没有法典的地方，这个词组覆盖群体内有约束力的规则。

senses.title: Oral poetry and performance
senses.definition: verse composed and re-performed aloud with formulaic phrases and music
senses.definitionCN: 以套语与音乐在口头创作并反复表演的韵文
senses.example: Homeric oral tradition was built on repeated epithets and fixed metres.
senses.exampleCN: 荷马式的口头传统建立在重复的修饰语与固定格律之上。
senses.why: In performance the text is recreated each time, so the phrase also names a poetic technique rather than a mere source.
senses.whyCN: 在表演中文本每次都被重新创造，因此这个词组也命名一种诗歌技艺，而不只是素材来源。

senses.title: The stage before writing
senses.definition: the period in a culture's history when knowledge circulated only by speech
senses.definitionCN: 一个文化史上知识只靠言谈流通的时期
senses.example: Scholars debate what oral tradition preserved before the first scripts.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们争论在最早的文字之前口头传统保存了什么。
senses.why: The phrase can mark a chronological stage, set against the moment a society begins to write.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组可以标记一个时间阶段，与社会开始书写的时刻相对。

senses.title: The reliability debate
senses.definition: the argument over whether spoken memory can be trusted as historical evidence
senses.definitionCN: 关于口头记忆能否作为历史证据被信任的争论
senses.example: The reliability debate treats oral tradition as testimony to be tested, not dismissed.
senses.exampleCN: 可靠性之争把口头传统当作有待检验的证言，而不是一概否定。
senses.why: Because memory reshapes what it keeps, the phrase also names the scholarly quarrel about its evidential value.
senses.whyCN: 因为记忆会重塑它所保存的东西，这个词组也命名关于其证据价值的学术争论。

intro.en: Oral comes from Latin os 'mouth' through oralis; tradition comes from Latin traditio 'a handing over', from tradere 'to hand across'. The English phrase was fixed as a folklore term in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: oral 经拉丁 oralis 来自 os「嘴」；tradition 来自拉丁 traditio「递交」，源自动词 tradere「交过去」。这个英语词组在十八、十九世纪作为民俗学术语固定下来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Os (genitive oris) meant 'mouth'. Oralis 'of the mouth' gave English oral. The deeper origin of os is not established.
items.cn: os（属格 oris）意为「嘴」。oralis「嘴的」给出英语 oral。os 更深的来源未得到证明。

items.en: Tradere 'to hand over, deliver, betray' is transparently trans- 'across' plus dare 'to give'.
items.cn: tradere「递交、交付、出卖」由表示「穿过」的前缀加 dare「给」构成，结构清楚。

items.en: Traditio named the act of handing something over, and already meant the teaching passed from one generation to the next.
items.cn: traditio 指递交的动作，并且已经表示一代传给下一代的教学内容。

items.en: Old French tradicion carried the word into English in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries, spelling it first with -cioun.
items.cn: 古法语 tradicion 在十二、十三世纪把该词带入英语，早期拼作 -cioun 结尾。

items.en: From the eighteenth century, oral tradition became a standard label for material circulating by speech, as antiquarians began to collect ballads and tales.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，oral tradition 成为靠言谈流通的材料的标准标签，古物研究者开始收集歌谣与故事。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of os is unknown, and the exact date at which the English pairing became a fixed term cannot be pinned down.
items.cn: 来源不确定：os 在拉丁语之前的来源不明，英语这一搭配固定为术语的确切年代也无法确定。

note.en: Group one is about sound and spelling confusions; group two holds neighbours in folklore and history.
note.cn: 第一组是读音与拼写上的混淆；第二组是民俗学与史学中的近邻词。

entries.definition: Of the ear or hearing. It sounds exactly like oral but refers to ears, not mouths.
entries.definitionCN: 关于耳朵或听觉的。读音与 oral 完全相同，却指耳朵，不指嘴。

entries.definition: Spoken rather than written; alone it can describe an exam, a report or a medicine taken by mouth.
entries.definitionCN: 口头的而非书面的；单用时也可指口试、口头报告或口服药物。

entries.definition: Anything handed down; alone it does not say whether the channel was speech or writing.
entries.definitionCN: 任何被传下来的东西；单用时并不说明通道是口说还是书写。

entries.definition: One who hands over something to an enemy. It descends from the same Latin verb 'to hand over' but took the meaning of betrayal.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西交给敌人的人。它源出同一个表示「递交」的拉丁动词，却走上了「背叛」一义。

entries.definition: Recorded personal testimony gathered by interview; it is the modern, documented end of the same field.
entries.definitionCN: 通过访谈采集并录音的个人证言；它是同一领域里现代且有记录的一端。

entries.definition: The tales, beliefs and customs of a people, whether or not they are told orally.
entries.definitionCN: 一个民族的故事、信仰与习俗，不论是否以口说方式讲述。

entries.definition: The activity of telling stories; it names the performance, not the inherited body.
entries.definitionCN: 讲故事的活动；它命名表演行为，而非继承下来的整体。

entries.definition: A near variant stressing speech; oral tradition is the established scholarly term.
entries.definitionCN: 强调口语的近义变体；oral tradition 才是学界固定术语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin parts, real folklore terms and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件、真实的民俗学术语与真实的固定说法。

normal.en: Oral points at the mouth; aural points at the ear; the two are pronounced alike, so spelling decides.
normal.cn: oral 指向嘴，aural 指向耳；两词读音相同，靠拼写分辨。

normal.en: Tradition is a handing over: the same Latin verb gives traitor, one who hands something to the enemy.
normal.cn: tradition 是递交：同一个拉丁动词还给出 traitor，即把东西交给敌人的人。

normal.en: The phrase needs no writing at all: voice, memory and repetition are the whole apparatus.
normal.cn: 这个词组完全不需要文字：嗓音、记忆与复述就是全部装置。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the field: preserve an oral tradition, pass down by oral tradition, oral tradition and written record.
normal.cn: 固定说法划出领域：保存口头传统、通过口头传统传下来、口头传统与书面记录。

normal.en: The plural oral traditions is common when different communities are compared.
normal.cn: 比较不同群体时，复数 oral traditions 很常用。

abstract.en: Picture a story that has no original, only a chain of tellers each handing it to the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一个没有原件的故事，只有一串讲述者，每人把它交给下一位。

abstract.en: Picture memory as a room that rearranges the furniture every time someone walks through.
abstract.cn: 想象记忆是一间屋子，每次有人走过，家具就被重新摆一遍。

abstract.en: Picture a library whose shelves are other people's heads.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，它的书架是别人的脑袋。

examples.en: The oral tradition preserved the names of the first settlers for six generations.
examples.cn: 口头传统把最早定居者的名字保存了六代。

examples.en: Fieldworkers recorded an oral tradition that was already fading.
examples.cn: 田野工作者记录下了一种正在消逝的口头传统。

examples.en: Written law replaced oral tradition only gradually in the highlands.
examples.cn: 在高地，成文法只是逐渐取代了口头传统。

dict_mnemonic.text: oral（嘴的）+ tradition（递交）＝ 用嘴一代代交下去的东西；记「不落纸，只落嘴」。

root: oral 源自拉丁 os「嘴」，属格为 oris，更早来源不确定，经形容词 oralis 进入英语；tradition 源自拉丁 traditio「递交」，来自动词 tradere，该动词由前缀表「穿过」加 dare「给」构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses track the same voice from a whole culture's inheritance down to a single family's version, then to method, law, performance, chronology and the argument over evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一个嗓音展开：从整个文化的继承，到一户人家的版本，再到方法、法律、表演、时间阶段与证据之争。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice in firelight handing a story to the next pair of ears.
core.cn: 核心意象：火光里的一个嗓音，把故事交给下一双耳朵。

branches.en: BODY AND CHANNEL: what is handed on, and the speaking that hands it on.
branches.cn: 整体与通道：被交下来的是什么，以及交它的言说方式。

branches.en: ONE LINEAGE'S VERSION: the same channel narrowed to a family's own account.
branches.cn: 一个世系的版本：同一通道收窄为一户人家的说法。

branches.en: TAPE RECORDER: spoken memory becomes evidence once it is recorded and cited.
branches.cn: 录音机：口传记忆一旦被录下并引用，就成了证据。

branches.en: BINDING RULES AND EARLY TIME: recitation can hold law, and the phrase can mark the age before writing.
branches.cn: 有约束力的规则与早期时段：诵说可以承载法律，这个词组也能标记文字之前的年代。

branches.en: PERFORMANCE AND DOUBT: the poem is recreated each telling, which is exactly why its reliability is argued.
branches.cn: 表演与怀疑：诗在每次讲述中都被重新创造，这也正是其可靠性被争论的原因。

intro.en: The phrase is a modern English combination of two Latin borrowings, one naming the mouth and one naming the act of handing over.
intro.cn: 这个词组是两个拉丁借词的现代英语组合，一个命名嘴，一个命名递交的动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin os, oralis and traditio, tradere supply every morpheme in the phrase; no Greek element is involved.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 os、oralis 与 traditio、tradere 提供了词组中的全部语素，不涉及希腊成分。

items.example: The tribe kept an oral record of the treaty.
items.exampleCN: 这个部落对那项条约保留了口头记录。

items.example: The agreement was made orally.
items.exampleCN: 这项约定是口头达成的。

items.example: The dance is a local tradition.
items.exampleCN: 这种舞蹈是一项地方传统。

items.meaningCN: 传统的；属于传下来的做法
items.example: They wore traditional dress at the festival.
items.exampleCN: 他们在节日穿传统服装。

items.meaning: attachment to old ways as a principle
items.meaningCN: 传统主义；以守旧为原则
items.example: His traditionalism resisted every reform.
items.exampleCN: 他的传统主义抵制一切改革。

items.meaning: a person who defends old ways
items.meaningCN: 传统主义者；维护旧法的人
items.example: The traditionalists rejected the new calendar.
items.exampleCN: 传统主义者拒绝新历法。

items.meaningCN: 口述史；录音的个人证言
items.example: The archive holds hundreds of oral history tapes.
items.exampleCN: 档案馆藏有数百盘口述史录音。

items.meaning: a person who keeps a tradition alive
items.meaningCN: 传统传承人；让传统活着的人
items.example: The last tradition bearer died in the village.
items.exampleCN: 最后一位传统传承人死在了村里。

latinEntries.structure: os (n., Latin, third declension; genitive oris)

definition_zh: 书写传统；以文字记录并延续的文本、知识与规范；书面传承本身
definition_en: the body of texts, and the practice of recording knowledge in writing, that a community carries forward
core_image: 一叠手抄本从书库传到抄书人案头，每一页都被重新誊写，页边添上新的批注
scene: 抄书人把旧手稿摊在案上，一笔一笔誊写，页边添上自己的批注，然后交给下一座书库。A written tradition preserved the wording exactly, even when the meaning drifted.
sceneCN: 这里 written tradition 指以文字记录并延续的文本与做法（第 1 个义项：作为整体传统）；句意为书写传统把措辞原样保存下来，即使意思已经漂移。

pos.zh: 书写传统（可数，指某一群体的文本传统；不可数，指书面传承方式）

collocations.phrase: the written tradition of the church

derivatives.zh: 书写（古英语 writan「刻划、描画」，是本词组的基础动词）
写作者（由基础动词加表施事者的名词后缀而来，由动作转指施事的人）
书写；文字作品（由基础动词加表活动或产物的名词后缀而来，由动作转指活动或其产物）
令状；书面命令（古英语同一词形的直接继承，由「写下的东西」转指法律文书）
书面的（由基础动词的过去分词转作形容词，由动作转指已成文的状态）

senses.title: The carried body of texts
senses.definition: the whole collection of documents, books and records that a community keeps and passes on
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体保存并代代相传的全部文书、书籍与记录
senses.example: The monastery's written tradition fills forty cabinets.
senses.exampleCN: 这座修道院的书写传统装了四十个柜子。
senses.why: Tradition names what is handed down; written fixes the medium. Together they name a body of documents rather than one book.
senses.whyCN: 前者指被传下的东西，后者限定媒介；合起来命名的是一批文件，而不是某一本书。

senses.title: The practice of recording
senses.definition: the habit of committing events, rules and knowledge to writing
senses.definitionCN: 把事件、规则与知识写下来的习惯
senses.example: A strong written tradition began when the court hired full-time clerks.
senses.exampleCN: 当宫廷雇了专职书吏，一种强固的书写传统就开始了。
senses.why: Here the phrase names the activity rather than its products: the act of writing is what carries knowledge forward.
senses.whyCN: 这里命名的是活动而非产物：正是书写这个动作把知识带向未来。

senses.title: A canon or lineage of texts
senses.definition: a recognised set of authoritative texts that later writers comment on and inherit
senses.definitionCN: 一套被承认的权威文本，后来的写作者对它注释并继承
senses.example: Later poets measured themselves against the written tradition of the epic.
senses.exampleCN: 后来的诗人以史诗的书写传统来衡量自己。
senses.why: Once texts are fixed, they can be ranked and commented on, and the phrase comes to mean a canon with a family tree.
senses.whyCN: 文本一旦固定，就能被排序与注释，这个词组于是指一棵有家谱的经典谱系。

senses.title: Legal and administrative records
senses.definition: the documentary habit of courts, temples and offices that keeps decisions in writing
senses.definitionCN: 法庭、神庙与官署把决定留在纸面上的文书习惯
senses.example: Land disputes were settled by consulting the written tradition of the county.
senses.exampleCN: 土地纠纷靠查阅该县的文书传统来解决。
senses.why: Administration needs a memory that outlives officials; written records supply exactly that, so the phrase covers archives of rule.
senses.whyCN: 行政需要一种比官员活得久的记忆；书面记录正好提供它，因此这个词组覆盖统治的档案。

senses.title: Scholarship built on citation
senses.definition: research that advances by quoting, correcting and adding to earlier written work
senses.definitionCN: 通过引用、修正与增补前人文字而推进的研究
senses.example: The field grew out of a written tradition of marginal notes.
senses.exampleCN: 这个领域从页边批注的书写传统中生长出来。
senses.why: Citation makes scholarship cumulative: each text stands on the page of another, and the phrase names that chain.
senses.whyCN: 引用使学术可以累积：每篇文字都站在另一篇的纸页上，这个词组命名的正是这条链。

senses.title: Literacy and print culture
senses.definition: the social stage in which reading and writing organise public life
senses.definitionCN: 阅读与书写组织公共生活的社会阶段
senses.example: Print turned a narrow written tradition into a mass one.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷把狭窄的书写传统变成了大众传统。
senses.why: The phrase can mark a whole social condition, set against an oral culture where most people never read.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组可以标记一整个社会状况，与多数人不识字的口头文化相对。

senses.title: Fixity of wording
senses.definition: the property that a text keeps the same words each time it is read
senses.definitionCN: 文本每次被阅读时都保持同样措辞的性质
senses.example: A written tradition can preserve a formula for a thousand years.
senses.exampleCN: 书写传统能把一个固定说法保存一千年。
senses.why: Writing freezes wording, so the phrase also names the exactness that speech cannot guarantee.
senses.whyCN: 书写冻结措辞，因此这个词组也命名言谈无法保证的那种精确。

senses.title: The critique of what writing leaves out
senses.titleCN: 对书写遗漏之物的批判
senses.definition: the argument that written records favour the literate, the powerful and the official
senses.definitionCN: 认为书面记录偏袒识字者、掌权者与官方视角的论点
senses.example: Historians now ask what the written tradition silenced.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学者现在会问书写传统让什么沉默了。
senses.why: Because only some voices reach the page, the phrase can also name the blind spot produced by writing itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为只有部分嗓音能到纸面，这个词组也能命名书写本身造成的盲区。

intro.en: Written is the past participle of write, from Old English writan 'to score, outline, scratch'. Tradition comes from Latin traditio 'a handing over'. The English phrase contrasts with oral tradition in folklore and classics. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: written 是 write 的过去分词，源自古英语 writan「刻划、描画、勾出轮廓」。tradition 来自拉丁 traditio「递交」。这个英语词组在民俗学与古典学中与口头传统相对。年代均为约数。

items.en: Writan was a strong verb meaning 'to score, outline, draw the figure of', with past tense wrat and past participle writen. Its earliest sense was cutting marks into a surface.
items.cn: writan 是强变化动词，意为「刻划、勾轮廓、描画形状」，过去式 wrat，过去分词 writen。最早的意义是把痕迹刻进表面。

items.en: The reconstructed ancestor is *writan 'to tear, scratch', a reconstruction attested by the older Germanic forms rather than by any written record.
items.cn: 重构的祖词是 *writan「撕、抓、刻」，这一形式靠更早的日耳曼语形式推得，并无直接书证。

items.en: The usual reconstruction is *wreid- 'to cut, scratch'. The reconstruction is secure for Germanic but its links outside Germanic are not established.
items.cn: 通行的重构是 *wreid-「切、刻」。这一重构在日耳曼语内部较可靠，但与日耳曼语之外的关联尚未证实。

items.en: Tradere 'to hand over' is trans- 'across' plus dare 'to give'; its noun traditio first meant delivery and then teaching handed down.
items.cn: tradere「递交」由表示「穿过」的前缀加 dare「给」构成；其名词 traditio 先指交付，再指传下的教导。

items.en: Written tradition became a standard counterpart to oral tradition in the nineteenth century, when collectors and classicists compared literate and spoken cultures.
items.cn: 十九世纪，written tradition 成为 oral tradition 的标准对应说法，当时收集者与古典学者开始比较文字文化与口说文化。

items.en: Source uncertain: the shape of the reconstructed Indo-European root is a reconstruction, and the older history of tradere's components beyond the transparent prefix and verb is not recoverable.
items.cn: 来源不确定：所重构的原始印欧语词根形状属重构形式；tradere 除清楚可见的前缀与动词外，更早的构件历史已不可考。

note.en: Group one separates forms of the verb write; group two holds textual and archival neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组区分动词 write 的各种形式；第二组是文本与档案方面的近邻词。

entries.definition: The act of writing or the marks produced; it can name a single piece of work, not an inherited body.
entries.definitionCN: 书写动作或写出的痕迹；可以指单件作品，而非继承的整体。

entries.definition: The past participle used as an adjective: put down on paper. It describes a thing, not a tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词：写在纸上的。它描述某物，而非一种传统。

entries.definition: A formal written order from a court; the spelling lost the final e and narrowed to law.
entries.definitionCN: 法庭的正式书面命令；拼写丢了词尾的 e，词义收窄到法律。

entries.definition: One who writes; the suffix marks the agent, while the phrase marks the inherited corpus.
entries.definitionCN: 写作的人；后缀标记施事，而词组标记继承下来的文本总体。

entries.definition: The chain of hand-copied copies through which a text survives; narrower than written tradition, which includes print.
entries.definitionCN: 文本靠手抄副本延续的链条；比书写传统窄，后者还包括印刷。

entries.definition: The study of how a text's wording changed across copies; it focuses on variants rather than on writing as a habit.
entries.definitionCN: 研究文本措辞在各副本间如何变化；它关注异文，而非书写习惯本身。

entries.definition: The social world shaped by movable type; it is a later stage within a written tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 由活字印刷塑造的社会世界；它是书写传统内部较晚的阶段。

entries.definition: The individual documents left behind; the tradition is the continuing practice that produced them.
entries.definitionCN: 留下的具体文件；而传统是产生这些文件的持续做法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Old English verb, its surviving forms and real archival phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的古英语动词、它留存的形式与真实的档案说法。

normal.en: Write first meant to scratch a mark; writing began as cutting, not as ink.
normal.cn: write 最初意为刻痕；书写一开始是刻，而不是蘸墨。

normal.en: The same verb yields writer, writing, writ and written, each pointing at a different part of the act.
normal.cn: 同一个动词给出 writer、writing、writ、written，各自指向动作的不同部分。

normal.en: Tradition is a handing over, so a written tradition is a handing over done on paper.
normal.cn: tradition 是递交，所以书写传统就是在纸上完成的递交。

normal.en: Fixed phrases set the contrast: written tradition and oral memory, a long written tradition.
normal.cn: 固定说法建立对比：书写传统与口头记忆、悠久的书写传统。

normal.en: The plural written traditions fits comparisons between churches, courts or schools.
normal.cn: 比较教会、宫廷或学派时，复数 written traditions 合适。

abstract.en: Picture a page that never forgets but also never notices who was left out.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸，它从不遗忘，却也从不注意谁被漏掉了。

abstract.en: Picture a chain of copyists, each adding one marginal note that later readers treat as part of the text.
abstract.cn: 想象一串抄写者，每人添一条页边批注，后来的读者却把它当作正文的一部分。

abstract.en: Picture a law that outlives every official who wrote it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条法律，比写下它的每位官员都活得久。

examples.en: The island's written tradition begins with ships' logs and church registers.
examples.cn: 这座岛的书写传统始于航海日志与教会登记簿。

examples.en: A written tradition can preserve a name long after the language around it changes.
examples.cn: 书写传统能在周围语言改变很久之后仍保存一个名字。

examples.en: Critics ask whose voices never entered the written tradition.
examples.cn: 批评者追问哪些人的声音从未进入书写传统。

dict_mnemonic.text: written（写下的）+ tradition（递交）＝ 用文字一页页交下去的东西；记「刻痕变墨迹，墨迹变档案」。

root: written 源自古英语 writan「刻划、描画」，其过去分词为 written，更早的日耳曼语与原始印欧语形式均属重构；tradition 源自拉丁 traditio「递交」，来自动词 tradere，该动词由前缀表「穿过」加 dare「给」构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the corpus itself to the habit of writing, then to canon, archive, scholarship, literacy, fixity and the criticism of what the page excludes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从文本总体移向书写习惯，再到经典、档案、学术、识字、固定性，以及对纸页排除之物的批判。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand copying a page so that the same words arrive in a later century.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手誊抄一页，让同样的字句抵达另一个世纪。

branches.en: CORPUS AND HABIT: the collected texts, and the repeated act of writing them down.
branches.cn: 总体与习惯：收集起来的文本，以及反复把它们写下的动作。

branches.en: CANON AND FIXITY: ranking texts requires that their wording stop changing.
branches.cn: 经典与固定：要给文本排序，先得让措辞不再变动。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: courts and offices keep decisions alive on paper.
branches.cn: 账册：法庭与官署靠纸面让决定继续活着。

branches.en: CITATION: scholarship grows by standing each text on the page of another.
branches.cn: 引用：学术靠让每篇文字站上另一篇的纸页而生长。

branches.en: LITERACY AND ITS BLIND SPOT: a reading public, and the voices that never reached it.
branches.cn: 识字及其盲区：一个阅读公众，以及从未抵达它的那些声音。

intro.en: The phrase combines an Old English verb with a Latin noun: the first half is native, the second borrowed.
intro.cn: 这个词组把古英语动词与拉丁名词组合起来：前半是本族语，后半是借词。

latinIntro.en: Only tradition is Latin; write and its forms descend from Old English and have no Latin source.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 tradition 属拉丁来源；write 及其各种形式源自古英语，没有拉丁来源。

items.meaning: to make marks that record words
items.meaningCN: 书写；留下记录文字的痕迹
items.example: She writes in a small notebook every night.
items.exampleCN: 她每晚在一个小本子上写字。

items.example: The writer revised the chapter twice.
items.exampleCN: 作者把这一章改了两遍。

items.meaning: the act of writing or what is written
items.example: His writing is clear and compact.
items.exampleCN: 他的文字清楚而紧凑。

items.example: A written answer is required.
items.exampleCN: 要求提交书面答复。

items.example: The court issued a writ of summons.
items.exampleCN: 法庭发出了传唤令状。

items.example: The tradition dates from the first abbey.
items.exampleCN: 这一传统始于第一座修道院。

items.example: Traditional records were kept in Latin.
items.exampleCN: 传统记录用拉丁文保存。

items.example: Monks transcribed the old pages by hand.
items.exampleCN: 修士们手工誊写那些旧页。

items.example: The manuscript survived in one copy.
items.exampleCN: 这份手稿只靠一个副本留存。

definition_zh: 文化保护；对遗产、语言、技艺与场所的保存与延续；使文化实践不在代际间断绝的整体工作
definition_en: the work of keeping a community's heritage, languages, skills and places from being lost
core_image: 修复室里，老师傅用旧法调漆补上木雕缺口，旁边的青年把每一步记进本子
scene: 修复室里，老师傅按旧法调漆补上木雕的缺口，青年在旁把每一步记进本子，好让下次有人照着做。Cultural preservation kept both the carving and the knowledge of how to repair it.
sceneCN: 这里 cultural preservation 指让遗产、技艺与相关知识不在代际间断绝的整体工作（第 1 个义项：作为整体工作）；句意为文化保护同时保住了木雕和修复它的手艺。

pos.zh: 文化保护（不可数，指这项工作；可数时指一项项保护行动）

derivatives.zh: 保存；保护（由拉丁 praeservare 经古法语进入，核心是「提前守住」，是本词组的基础动词）
保存；保护（由基础动词加表过程或结果的名词后缀而来，由动作转指过程）
防腐剂（由基础动词加表功能的形容词后缀而来，由动作转指起保存作用的东西）
保护者；保存者（由基础动词加表施事者的名词后缀而来，由动作转指施事的人或物）
文化的（由基础名词加表属性的形容词后缀而来，由「耕作、培养」转指「属于文化」）

senses.title: The whole undertaking
senses.definition: the combined work of keeping a community's heritage, practices and knowledge alive
senses.definitionCN: 让一个群体的遗产、实践与知识继续存活的综合工作
senses.example: Cultural preservation is cheaper than rebuilding a lost archive.
senses.exampleCN: 文化保护比重建一座被毁的档案馆更便宜。
senses.why: The phrase names an undertaking rather than one method: many kinds of care are gathered under a single heading.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组命名的是一项事业，而非单一方法：许多种照料被归在同一个名目之下。

senses.title: Conserving objects and sites
senses.definition: restoring and protecting buildings, crafts and objects so that their material form survives
senses.definitionCN: 修复与保护建筑、器物与工艺品，使其物质形态得以留存
senses.example: Cultural preservation stabilized the wall paintings before the roof was fixed.
senses.exampleCN: 文化保护工作先稳住了壁画，再修屋顶。
senses.why: Heritage has a body, and bodies decay; preservation begins with stopping that decay in stone, wood and pigment.
senses.whyCN: 遗产有身体，而身体会朽坏；保护首先是在石头、木头与颜料上止住这种朽坏。

senses.title: Keeping languages alive
senses.definition: supporting the daily use and teaching of a language that would otherwise lose its speakers
senses.definitionCN: 支持一种语言的日常使用与教学，使其不至于失去使用者
senses.example: Language nests are a form of cultural preservation that works through children.
senses.exampleCN: 语言巢是通过儿童来运作的一种文化保护形式。
senses.why: A language dies when it stops being spoken at home, so preservation here means creating occasions for speech, not archiving tapes.
senses.whyCN: 一种语言在家里不再被说就会死，所以这里的保护意味着创造说话的机会，而不只是存录音。

senses.title: Documenting before loss
senses.definition: recording songs, recipes, techniques and vocabularies while their practitioners are still alive
senses.definitionCN: 在传承人还在世时，把歌谣、食谱、工艺与词汇录下来
senses.example: Cultural preservation teams spent the winter filming basket weaving.
senses.exampleCN: 文化保护团队花了一个冬天拍摄编篮工艺。
senses.why: When the carrier of a skill dies, the skill can vanish in one generation; documentation buys time and creates a reference.
senses.whyCN: 一项技艺的承载者去世，技艺可能在一代内消失；记录争取时间，并留下可查的参照。

senses.title: Institutional policy
senses.definition: the work of museums, archives, ministries and international bodies that fund and regulate protection
senses.definitionCN: 博物馆、档案馆、文化部门与国际机构出资并规范保护工作的那一套实践
senses.example: National cultural preservation law protects the old town from demolition.
senses.exampleCN: 国家文化保护法保护老城免遭拆除。
senses.why: Private care is fragile, so the phrase often names the public machinery of budgets, listings and permits.
senses.whyCN: 私人的照料很脆弱，因此这个词组常指预算、名录与许可构成的那套公共机器。

senses.title: Community-led continuity
senses.definition: protection carried out by the community itself as a living practice rather than a frozen exhibit
senses.definitionCN: 由社区自身作为活着的实践来进行的保护，而不是做成冻结的展品
senses.example: Cultural preservation works best when the community decides what matters.
senses.exampleCN: 当由社区决定什么重要时，文化保护效果最好。
senses.why: A practice stays alive only if people still want to do it; this sense shifts the agent from experts to bearers.
senses.whyCN: 一种实践只有人们还愿意做才活着；这个义项把行动者从专家转到了传承人。

senses.title: Digital archiving
senses.definition: using scans, recordings and databases to keep and share cultural material
senses.definitionCN: 用扫描、录音与数据库保存并共享文化材料
senses.example: Digital cultural preservation put the scroll online without touching it.
senses.exampleCN: 数字文化保护让卷轴上线，却不必触碰原件。
senses.why: A copy that anyone can open protects the original from handling and extends access beyond the museum.
senses.whyCN: 人人都能打开的副本既让原件免于被触摸，也把访问延伸到博物馆之外。

senses.title: The contested question of whose culture
senses.definition: the critical reading that preservation can freeze, exoticise or dispossess the people it claims to help
senses.definitionCN: 一种批判读法：保护可能冻结、异域化或剥夺它声称要帮助的人
senses.example: Cultural preservation became a land dispute when the site was fenced.
senses.exampleCN: 当遗址被围起来，文化保护就变成了一场土地争端。
senses.why: Choosing what to keep is choosing whose version counts, so the phrase also names a field of conflict.
senses.whyCN: 选择保存什么，就是选择谁的版本算数，因此这个词组也命名一片冲突之地。

intro.en: Culture comes from Latin cultura 'cultivation', from colere 'to till, inhabit, honour'; preservation comes from Latin praeservare 'to keep safe in advance'. The English phrase became a policy term in the twentieth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: culture 来自拉丁 cultura「耕作、培养」，源自动词 colere「耕作、居住、敬奉」；preservation 来自拉丁 praeservare「提前守住」。这个英语词组在二十世纪成为政策术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Colere meant 'to till, cultivate, dwell in, and worship'. Its root is usually connected with a verb for turning or moving around, but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: colere 意为「耕作、培养、居住、敬奉」。其词根通常与表示「转动、绕行」的动词联系起来，但这一重构并不确定。

items.en: Cultura first meant the tilling of land, then care and training of the mind; Cicero already speaks of a culture of the soul.
items.cn: cultura 先指土地的耕作，再指对心智的照料与训练；西塞罗已经说到灵魂的培养。

items.en: Praeservare is prae- 'before, in advance' plus servare 'to keep, guard'. Servare's deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: praeservare 由表示「预先」的前缀加 servare「看守、保存」构成。servare 更深的来源未得到证明。

items.en: Culture entered English through Old French in the fifteenth century; preserve came through Old French preserver, and preservation followed in the sixteenth.
items.cn: culture 在十五世纪经古法语进入英语；preserve 经古法语 preserver 进入，preservation 在十六世纪随后出现。

items.en: In the twentieth century cultural preservation became the language of museums, ministries and international conventions, especially after the 1972 World Heritage Convention.
items.cn: 二十世纪，cultural preservation 成为博物馆、文化部门与国际公约的语言，尤其在1972年《世界遗产公约》之后。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of both colere and servare is unsettled, and the modern broadening of culture to 'a whole way of life' is generally dated to the nineteenth century rather than to Latin.
items.cn: 来源不确定：colere 与 servare 在拉丁语之前的来源均无定论；culture 现代扩展为「整套生活方式」一般追溯到十九世纪，而非拉丁语本身。

note.en: Group one separates the preserve family; group two holds neighbouring terms in heritage work.
note.cn: 第一组区分 preserve 词族；第二组是遗产工作中的近邻术语。

entries.definition: The act of keeping something safe; alone it can refer to food, buildings or documents, with no mention of culture.
entries.definitionCN: 保存某物的动作；单用时可指食物、建筑或文件，与「文化」无关。

entries.definition: A chemical that stops food from decaying; the suffix marks a thing that preserves, not the work as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 防止食物腐败的化学物质；后缀标记起保存作用的东西，而非整体工作。

entries.definition: Protection of nature or of artefacts, built on a different Latin verb meaning 'to keep whole'; it often stresses careful management.
entries.definitionCN: 对自然或文物的保护，来自另一个意为「保持完整」的拉丁动词；常强调谨慎的管理。

entries.definition: Refined or educated; the suffix turns the noun toward a personal quality, not a heritage.
entries.definitionCN: 有教养的；后缀把名词转向个人品质，而非遗产。

entries.definition: The planning and administration of heritage sites; it is the institutional side of cultural preservation.
entries.definitionCN: 对遗产场所的规划与行政；它是文化保护的机构化一面。

entries.definition: The term used in UNESCO documents for protecting intangible practices; narrower and more legalistic.
entries.definitionCN: 联合国教科文组织文件里保护非物质实践的说法；更窄，也更法律化。

entries.definition: Bringing a declining language back into daily use; it is one strand within cultural preservation.
entries.definitionCN: 让衰落的语言回到日常使用；它是文化保护中的一条支线。

entries.definition: Storing records and materials for future use; it is a tool of preservation rather than its whole aim.
entries.definitionCN: 为将来使用而储存记录与材料；它是保护的工具，而非全部目的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin parts, real policy phrases and real institutional terms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件、真实的政策说法与真实的机构术语。

normal.en: Culture began as tilling the soil; preserving culture is tending something that grows, not embalming it.
normal.cn: culture 起初是耕地；保护文化是照料会生长之物，而不是把它做成标本。

normal.en: Preserve carries 'before': the point is to act before the loss happens.
normal.cn: preserve 含着「预先」：要点是在失去发生之前动手。

normal.en: The same family gives preserve, preservation, preservative and preserver.
normal.cn: 同一词族给出 preserve、preservation、preservative、preserver。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the field: cultural preservation efforts, cultural preservation policy, community-led cultural preservation.
normal.cn: 固定说法划出领域：文化保护工作、文化保护政策、社区主导的文化保护。

normal.en: Culture is uncountable here, while preservations can count individual actions.
normal.cn: 这里 culture 不可数，而 preservations 可以数一项项行动。

abstract.en: Picture a cracked bowl being mended with the same clay and the same method that made it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只裂了的碗，用当初制它的同一种泥、同一种手法补好。

abstract.en: Picture a language kept alive by a kitchen table rather than by a dictionary.
abstract.cn: 想象一种语言靠一张饭桌活着，而不是靠一本词典。

abstract.en: Picture a museum that asks the community what it may keep.
abstract.cn: 想象一座博物馆，先去问社区它可以保留什么。

examples.en: Cultural preservation failed because nobody had taught the repair technique to the young.
examples.cn: 文化保护失败了，因为没人把这门修复技术教给年轻人。

examples.en: The festival is cultural preservation carried out by dancing, not by writing reports.
examples.cn: 这个节日是靠跳舞、而不是靠写报告进行的文化保护。

examples.en: Digital cultural preservation made the fragile atlas readable in every school.
examples.cn: 数字文化保护让那本脆弱的地图册在每所学校都能读。

dict_mnemonic.text: culture（耕作、培养）+ preservation（预先守住）＝ 在失去之前把会生长的东西照看住；记「先修屋顶，再谈展览」。

root: cultural 源自拉丁 cultura「耕作、培养」，来自动词 colere「耕作、居住、敬奉」，更早词根存疑；preservation 源自拉丁 praeservare「提前守住」，由前缀表「预先」加 servare「看守、保存」构成，servare 更深的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the whole undertaking through objects, languages, documentation, policy and community practice to digital copies and the quarrel over ownership.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从整体事业出发，经实物、语言、记录、政策与社区实践，走到数字副本与归属之争。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a broken object mended with the same clay, while a young hand writes down the method.
core.cn: 核心意象：用同一种泥修补破器，同时有一双年轻的手把方法记下。

branches.en: THE WHOLE TASK AND THE OBJECT: an undertaking, then the stone and wood that decay.
branches.cn: 整体任务与对象：先是一项事业，再是会朽坏的石头与木头。

branches.en: THE SPOKEN LIFE: a language survives only while it is used at home.
branches.cn: 口说的生命：语言只有还在家里被使用才活着。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF COPY: a recording made in time, and a scan that anyone can open.
branches.cn: 两种副本：及时录下的记录，以及任何人都能打开的扫描件。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC MACHINE: budgets, listings and permits decide what gets care.
branches.cn: 公共机器：预算、名录与许可决定什么能得到照料。

branches.en: WHO CONTINUES IT: the community as bearer, and the conflict over whose version is kept.
branches.cn: 由谁延续：社区作为传承者，以及关于保存谁版本的冲突。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin noun for cultivation to a Latin noun for guarding beforehand; both parts still build common English words.
intro.cn: 这个词组把表示「耕作、培养」的拉丁名词与表示「预先看守」的拉丁名词结合起来，两部分在英语中仍能构成常用词。

latinIntro.en: Latin colere and cultura supply the first element; prae- and servare supply the second. No Greek element is involved.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 colere 与 cultura 提供前一成分；prae- 与 servare 提供后一成分，不涉及希腊成分。

items.meaning: the shared way of life of a people
items.meaningCN: 一个民族共享的生活方式
items.example: The island has a distinct culture of its own.
items.exampleCN: 这座岛有自己独特的文化。

items.meaning: of a people's shared way of life
items.example: Cultural ties survived the border change.
items.exampleCN: 文化纽带在边界变动后仍然存在。

items.example: Farmers cultivated rice on the terraces.
items.exampleCN: 农民在梯田上种稻。

items.meaning: the act of tilling or developing
items.example: Cultivation of the slope began centuries ago.
items.exampleCN: 这片坡地的耕作始于几个世纪前。

items.meaning: to keep from loss or decay
items.meaningCN: 保存；使免于损失或腐坏
items.example: They preserved the wooden roof with resin.
items.exampleCN: 他们用树脂保护木屋顶。

items.meaning: the work of keeping something safe
items.example: Preservation of the site took a decade.
items.exampleCN: 该遗址的保护花了十年。

items.example: Old inks contained no preservative.
items.exampleCN: 旧墨水里没有防腐剂。

items.meaning: a person or thing that preserves
items.example: She became the chief preserver of the songs.
items.exampleCN: 她成了这些歌的主要保存者。

items.meaningCN: 保护；保育（强调谨慎管理）
items.example: Stone conservation stopped the salt damage.
items.exampleCN: 石质保护止住了盐害。

items.meaning: one who cares for a collection
items.example: The curator planned the new gallery.
items.exampleCN: 策展人规划了新展厅。

latinEntries.meaning: to till, cultivate, dwell in, honour

definition_zh: 身份；自我认同；同一性（逻辑与数学中的「完全相同」）；群体特性；身份证明
definition_en: the fact of being the same, or the set of qualities by which a person or group is recognised as itself
core_image: 一张脸在两面镜子之间被比对：左边是记忆中的自己，右边是证件上的自己，中间写着同一个名字
scene: 过闸口时，守卫先看证件上的照片，再看她的脸，然后才把门打开。Her identity was checked twice before the gate opened.
sceneCN: 这里 identity 指一个人可被核验的身份（第 4 个义项：证件与法律意义上的身份）；句意为她的身份在闸口打开前被核对了两次。

pos.zh: 身份；自我认同（可数，指一个人的身份；不可数，指认同这一性质）
同一性；完全相同（逻辑、数学用法，不可数）
特性；群体特征（可数，指某一群体或品牌的辨识特征）

derivatives.zh: 辨认；确认（经法语 identifier 来自同一拉丁词根「同一」，由「视为同一」转指「认出是谁」）
识别；身份证明（由基础动词加表过程或结果的名词后缀而来，由动作转指过程与证件）
标识符；识别标记（由基础动词加表施事者或工具的名词后缀而来，由动作转指起识别作用的东西）
完全相同的（由中世纪拉丁同一词根加表属性的形容词后缀而来，与 identity 同根，由「同一」转指「毫无差别」）
完全相同地（由基础形容词加表方式的副词后缀而来，由性质转指方式）

senses.title: Being one and the same
senses.definition: the relation in which a thing is itself and not another thing
senses.definitionCN: 某物就是它自身而非另一物的关系
senses.example: Philosophers ask what makes identity hold across change.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家追问是什么让同一性在变化中保持。
senses.why: The Latin source means 'same'; the oldest sense is bare sameness, before any notion of a self.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁来源意为「同一」；最古老的义项是赤裸的相同，尚未涉及自我。

senses.title: Personal selfhood
senses.definition: the answer a person gives to the question of who they are
senses.definitionCN: 一个人对「我是谁」这一问题的回答
senses.example: Living abroad changed his identity more than his accent.
senses.exampleCN: 在海外生活改变他的自我认同，胜过改变他的口音。
senses.why: Sameness turns inward: to have an identity is to be able to say which self is mine.
senses.whyCN: 「同一」转向内部：拥有身份，就是能说出哪一个自我是我的。

senses.title: Continuity through time
senses.definition: the sense that a person or thing remains the same entity while changing
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或物在变化中仍是同一实体的感觉
senses.example: Memory is one thread that holds identity together over decades.
senses.exampleCN: 记忆是把身份在数十年间连起来的一根线。
senses.why: If sameness is to survive change, it must be carried by something continuous; Locke located that thread in memory.
senses.whyCN: 如果同一要穿越变化，就得有某种连续之物承载它；洛克把这根线放在记忆里。

senses.title: Legal and official identity
senses.definition: the recorded facts by which a state recognises a person, such as name, number and photograph
senses.definitionCN: 国家据以承认某人的记录事实，如姓名、号码与照片
senses.example: The border officer compared the face with the identity on the card.
senses.exampleCN: 边检人员把脸与卡片上的身份信息作了比对。
senses.why: Institutions need a verifiable version of a person, so identity becomes a document that can be checked.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要一个人可核验的版本，于是身份变成一份可以被检查的文件。

senses.title: Social category membership
senses.definition: the groups a person belongs to and is seen as belonging to, such as class, profession or religion
senses.definitionCN: 一个人所属并被看作所属的群体，如阶层、职业或宗教
senses.example: Work gave her a social identity she had lacked before.
senses.exampleCN: 工作给了她此前缺少的社会身份。
senses.why: People are also known by their places in society; identity then means the labels and memberships attached to a person.
senses.whyCN: 人也借其在社会中的位置被认识；身份于是指附着于人的标签与归属。

senses.title: A group's distinctiveness
senses.definition: the traits, memory and style by which a community recognises itself as different from others
senses.definitionCN: 一个共同体据以把自己与他者区分开的特征、记忆与风格
senses.example: The language became the core of the region's identity.
senses.exampleCN: 这门语言成了该地区群体特性的核心。
senses.why: The same word moves from one person to many: a group can also be said to be itself and not another.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词从一个人移到许多人：一个群体也可以被说成是它自身而非他者。

senses.title: Exact sameness of two terms
senses.definition: the statement that two expressions or objects are one and the same, often written with an equals sign
senses.definitionCN: 断言两个表达或对象是同一回事，常以等号表示
senses.example: In logic, identity is written with a double bar, not with a comma.
senses.exampleCN: 在逻辑中，同一性用双横线表示，而不是逗号。
senses.why: This is the first sense sharpened into a symbol: sameness asserted between two names.
senses.whyCN: 这是第一个义项的符号化：在两个名称之间断言同一。

senses.title: Mathematical identity
senses.definition: an equation that is true for every value of its variables
senses.definitionCN: 对其变量的一切取值都成立的等式
senses.example: The identity holds for every real number, not just for one.
senses.exampleCN: 这个恒等式对每个实数都成立，而不只对一个成立。
senses.why: In algebra sameness can be universal: two forms differ in appearance yet are the same value everywhere.
senses.whyCN: 在代数中，同一可以是普遍的：两个形式外观不同，却处处是同一个值。

senses.title: Corporate and brand identity
senses.definition: the designed set of signs, colours and tone by which an organisation is recognised
senses.definitionCN: 一个组织据以被识别的一套设计过的标志、颜色与语调
senses.example: The bank spent millions on a new identity after the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 合并之后，这家银行花巨资打造新的品牌识别。
senses.why: Marketing borrows the word for recognisability: a firm wants to be instantly itself in the eye of the public.
senses.whyCN: 营销借用了这个词来表示可辨识性：企业希望在公众眼里一眼就是它自己。

intro.en: Identity comes from Late Latin identitas 'sameness', an abstract noun built on idem 'the same'. The noun was coined in the fourth century to render a Greek philosophical term. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: identity 来自晚期拉丁 identitas「同一」，是由 idem「同一的」构成的抽象名词。该名词在四世纪被造出，用来对译一个希腊哲学术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Idem 'the same' is analysed as is 'he, it' plus a demonstrative particle -dem, the same element seen in quidem and tandem. The deeper origin of the pronoun is not established.
items.cn: idem「同一的」通常分析为 is「他、它」加指示性小品词 -dem，同一成分也见于 quidem 与 tandem。该代词更深的来源未得到证明。

items.en: Identitas was coined as an abstract noun for sameness, most often credited to Marius Victorinus in the fourth century, who needed a Latin word for Greek tautotes in theology.
items.cn: identitas 是表示「同一」的抽象名词，最常被归功于四世纪的马里乌斯·维克托里努斯，他需要用一个拉丁词来对译神学中的希腊 tautotes。

items.en: The word passed through Old French identite and entered English in the fifteenth century, first in the sense of absolute sameness.
items.cn: 该词经古法语 identite 在十五世纪进入英语，最初表示绝对的相同。

items.en: Locke's discussion of personal identity in the seventeenth century moved the word from sameness of substance to sameness of a conscious person over time.
items.cn: 洛克在十七世纪关于人格同一性的讨论，把该词从实体的相同转向一个有意识的人跨时间的同一。

items.en: In the 1950s Erikson gave identity its modern psychological sense: a felt continuity of self that an adolescent must assemble.
items.cn: 一九五零年代，埃里克森赋予 identity 现代心理学含义：一种青少年必须整合起来的、被体验到的自我连续性。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of the pronoun is, the identity of the scholar who coined identitas, and the exact route by which the word reached French are all less than certain.
items.cn: 来源不确定：代词 is 在拉丁语之前的来源、造出 identitas 的学者身份，以及该词抵达法语的确切路径，都不是完全确定的。

note.en: Group one separates the identify family; group two holds words for self and for sameness.
note.cn: 第一组区分 identify 词族；第二组是关于自我与相同的近邻词。

entries.definition: To establish who or what something is; it names the act of matching, not the matched self.
entries.definitionCN: 确认某人或某物是什么；它命名的是比对动作，而非被确认的自我。

entries.definition: The act of recognising, or the documents that prove who one is; it is a procedure and its instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 辨认的动作，或证明身份的文件；它是程序及其工具。

entries.definition: Exactly the same; the adjective stays with sameness and does not take on the sense of a self.
entries.definitionCN: 完全相同的；形容词停在「相同」一义，不承担「自我」义。

entries.definition: A name or code that marks something; it is an external tag, not the identity it points to.
entries.definitionCN: 标记某物的名称或代码；它是外部标签，而非它所指向的身份。

entries.definition: A person as conscious of their own being; it is the inner subject, while identity is the recognised pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 意识到自身存在的个人；它是内在主体，而身份是被辨识的模式。

entries.definition: The condition of being a person with a self; more abstract and less social than identity.
entries.definitionCN: 作为有自我之人的状态；比 identity 更抽象、更少社会性。

entries.definition: The moral or personal qualities of someone; identity answers 'who', character answers 'what kind'.
entries.definitionCN: 某人的道德或人格品质；身份回答「是谁」，性格回答「什么样」。

entries.definition: The role or face one presents to others; it is a mask-like version of identity, not the whole of it.
entries.definitionCN: 向他人呈现的角色或面孔；它是身份的面具式版本，而非全部。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pronoun, the real coinage and real modern compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁代词、真实的造词与真实的现代复合词。

normal.en: Identity begins as 'same': before it can mean who you are, it means being one thing.
normal.cn: identity 起初是「同一」：在能表示「你是谁」之前，它先表示「是同一个东西」。

normal.en: The family runs identify, identification, identifier, identical, identically.
normal.cn: 词族包括 identify、identification、identifier、identical、identically。

normal.en: Locke moved the word inward, Erikson moved it into psychology, and marketing took it outward again as brand identity.
normal.cn: 洛克把它转向内部，埃里克森把它带入心理学，营销又把它向外变成品牌识别。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the modern senses: sense of identity, identity crisis, identity theft, national identity.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出现代义：身份认同感、身份危机、身份盗用、民族认同。

normal.en: The plural identities is standard for several persons, groups or brands.
normal.cn: 指多个人、群体或品牌时，复数 identities 是标准用法。

abstract.en: Picture a rope made of many fibres: no single fibre is the rope, yet the rope is nothing but them.
abstract.cn: 想象一条由许多纤维组成的绳：没有一根纤维是绳，绳却只是它们。

abstract.en: Picture a face that keeps changing while the name on the door stays the same.
abstract.cn: 想象一张不断变化的脸，门上的名字却始终不变。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror that answers 'you' only because the person in front of it also answers 'you'.
abstract.cn: 想象一面镜子，它回答「你」，只因为站在它前面的人也回答「你」。

examples.en: The treaty recognised the tribe's identity as well as its land.
examples.cn: 这项条约既承认了部落的土地，也承认了它的群体身份。

examples.en: He applied for a new passport because his identity had been stolen.
examples.cn: 因为身份被盗用，他申请了新护照。

examples.en: In algebra an identity is true for all values, which is what makes it useful.
examples.cn: 在代数中，恒等式对一切取值都成立，这正是它有用之处。

dict_mnemonic.text: idem（同一）+ ity（性质）＝ 让一个东西始终是它自己的那种性质；记「同一件事，同一个我」。

root: 源自晚期拉丁 identitas「同一」，由 idem「同一的」加抽象名词后缀构成；idem 一般分析为 is「他、它」加指示性小品词，更早来源不确定。该名词在四世纪被造出，多归功于马里乌斯·维克托里努斯。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses begin with bare sameness, turn inward to a self and its continuity, then outward to documents, social categories, group traits, logic, algebra and brand design.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从赤裸的相同出发，转向内部的自我及其连续，再向外到证件、社会类别、群体特征、逻辑、代数与品牌设计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two mirrors facing each other, with one name written between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两面相对的镜子，中间写着一个名字。

branches.en: SAMENESS AT THREE STRICTNESSES: a thing is itself, two names may denote it, and a formula may hold for all values.
branches.cn: 三种严格度的同一：某物是它自身，两个名称可以同指，一个公式可以对一切取值成立。

branches.en: INWARD: the self that answers 'who', and the thread that keeps it the same across years.
branches.cn: 向内：回答「是谁」的自我，以及让它在岁月中保持同一的那根线。

branches.en: PAPER VERSION: the state keeps a checkable copy of the person.
branches.cn: 纸面版本：国家保存了一份可核验的个人副本。

branches.en: OUTWARD INTO SOCIETY: memberships attached to a person, then the same pattern at the scale of a group.
branches.cn: 向外进入社会：附着于个人的归属，再是同一模式在群体尺度上的表现。

branches.en: DESIGNED RECOGNITION: a firm manufactures the signs by which it is known.
branches.cn: 被设计的辨识：企业制造出让人认识它的那些符号。

intro.en: Identity is a Latin abstract noun whose stem also builds the identify family; the ending marks a quality or state.
intro.cn: identity 是拉丁抽象名词，其词干还构成 identify 一族；词尾标记一种性质或状态。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is idem 'same', with the abstract ending -itas. Medieval identicus gives identical, so the family is Latin throughout.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁基础是 idem「同一的」，加抽象词尾 -itas。中世纪拉丁 identicus 给出 identical，因此这一词族全程属拉丁来源。

items.meaning: to establish the sameness of; to recognise
items.example: Police identified the driver from the camera.
items.exampleCN: 警方通过摄像头确认了司机。

items.meaning: the act of recognising, or the proof used
items.example: Bring identification to the interview.
items.exampleCN: 面试时带上身份证明。

items.meaning: a code or label that marks something
items.example: Each sample carries a unique identifier.
items.exampleCN: 每个样本都有一个唯一标识符。

items.example: The twins wore identical coats.
items.exampleCN: 这对双胞胎穿着完全相同的外套。

items.example: Both machines were identically set.
items.exampleCN: 两台机器设置得完全相同。

items.meaning: a composite picture used by police
items.meaningCN: 拼图画像；警方用于辨认的合成照片
items.example: Witnesses helped build an identikit.
items.exampleCN: 目击者帮助拼出了画像。

items.meaning: an official document proving who one is
items.example: He showed his identity card at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 他在门口出示了身份证。

items.meaning: a person's own sense of who they are
items.example: Travel unsettled her self-identity.
items.exampleCN: 旅行动摇了她的自我认同。

definition_zh: 集体认同；一个群体共享的「我们」感及其自我界定；群体成员对共同归属的认知
definition_en: the shared sense of 'we' by which a group defines itself and its members recognise one another
core_image: 一群人围看同一张旧照片，指着里面的人说「这是我们」，照片外的人却认不出谁是谁
scene: 聚会时，一群人围着同一张旧照片，指着上面的人说这是我们的祖辈，而旁边做客的人只看见一排模糊的脸。A collective identity formed around the photograph long before anyone wrote the names down.
sceneCN: 这里 collective identity 指一个群体共享的「我们」感（第 1 个义项：共享归属感）；句意为围绕这张照片早已形成一种集体认同，远早于有人把名字写下来。

pos.zh: 集体认同（可数，指某一群体的认同；不可数，指这种共享归属的性质）

derivatives.zh: 收集；聚集（由拉丁 colligere 经法语进入，核心是「把东西聚到一起」，是本词组的动词基础）
收藏；收集（由基础动词加表过程或结果的名词后缀而来，由动作转指过程与藏品）
集体的（由基础动词加表性质的形容词后缀而来，由动作转指「属于一群人共同」的性质）
集体地（由基础形容词加表方式的副词后缀而来，由性质转指方式）
集体主义（由基础形容词加表主张的名词后缀而来，由性质转指主张）

senses.title: The felt 'we'
senses.definition: the shared feeling among members that they belong to one body with a common past and future
senses.definitionCN: 成员之间共享的感受：他们属于一个拥有共同过去与未来的整体
senses.example: The choir's collective identity grew out of years of Tuesday rehearsals.
senses.exampleCN: 合唱团的集体认同是在多年周二排练中长出来的。
senses.why: Identity is sameness recognised; collective applies it to many selves that feel themselves to be one body.
senses.whyCN: 前者是被辨认出的同一；后者把它施加到许多自我身上，这些自我感到自己是一个整体。

senses.title: Definition against others
senses.titleCN: 在与他人对照中界定自我
senses.definition: the boundary by which a group says what it is by saying what it is not
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体靠说明自己不是什么来界定自己是什么的那道边界
senses.example: The collective identity sharpened only after the neighbouring town claimed the same festival.
senses.exampleCN: 直到邻镇声称拥有同一个节日，这种集体认同才变得清晰。
senses.why: A 'we' needs a 'they'; the boundary is not an accident but the mechanism by which the group sees itself.
senses.whyCN: 「我们」需要一个「他们」；边界不是意外，而是群体看见自身的机制。

senses.title: A sociological concept
senses.definition: the shared representations, symbols and memories through which a society reproduces itself
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会借以自我再生产出来的共享表征、符号与记忆
senses.example: Durkheim treated collective identity as a fact sui generis, not a sum of private opinions.
senses.exampleCN: 涂尔干把集体认同当作一种自成一类的事实，而非私人意见的总和。
senses.why: The concept names a level of reality above individuals: shared symbols constrain what members can think and want.
senses.whyCN: 这一概念命名了高于个体的一个层面：共享符号约束着成员能想什么、要什么。

senses.title: National and political identity
senses.definition: the sense of belonging to a nation or political community, often built through schools, maps and ceremonies
senses.definitionCN: 归属于一个民族或政治共同体的感觉，常通过学校、地图与仪式建构
senses.example: Universal schooling gave the new state a collective identity within two generations.
senses.exampleCN: 普及教育在两代人之内给新国家造出了集体认同。
senses.why: Modern states need populations to imagine themselves as one; the phrase names that imagined unity.
senses.whyCN: 现代国家需要人口把自己想象成一个整体；这个词组命名的正是那种被想象的统一。

senses.title: Organizational identity
senses.definition: the shared understanding among employees of what their organisation is and stands for
senses.definitionCN: 员工对「本组织是什么、代表什么」的共享理解
senses.example: After the merger, the two firms struggled to form a single collective identity.
senses.exampleCN: 合并之后，两家公司难以形成单一的集体认同。
senses.why: The concept travels from nations to firms: any lasting body needs a story its members can share.
senses.whyCN: 这个概念从国家移到公司：任何持久的团体都需要一个成员可以共享的故事。

senses.title: Ethnic and religious belonging
senses.definition: the shared identity of an ethnic or religious community, carried by language, ritual and kinship
senses.definitionCN: 族群或宗教共同体的共享认同，由语言、仪式与亲属关系承载
senses.example: The diaspora kept its collective identity alive through Saturday schools.
senses.exampleCN: 侨居群体靠周末学校让集体认同活着。
senses.why: Where a group is scattered, ritual and schooling must do the work that shared ground once did.
senses.whyCN: 当群体分散各地，仪式与学校就必须承担曾经由共同土地承担的工作。

senses.title: Mobilised in a movement
senses.definition: a collective identity activated to claim rights, land or recognition in public conflict
senses.definitionCN: 在公共冲突中被激活、用以主张权利、土地或承认的集体认同
senses.example: The land case turned a quiet collective identity into a political force.
senses.exampleCN: 那场土地案件把一种沉默的集体认同变成了政治力量。
senses.why: Identity becomes visible when it is used: a shared 'we' can be turned into a claim on institutions.
senses.whyCN: 认同在被使用时才显形：共享的「我们」可以被转成对制度的主张。

senses.title: Constructed and contested
senses.definition: the critical view that collective identity is made, revised and disputed rather than given once for all
senses.definitionCN: 一种批判看法：集体认同是被制造、修订与争夺的，而非一次给定
senses.example: Historians show that the collective identity was assembled from borrowed pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学者表明，这种集体认同是由借来的碎片拼装而成。
senses.why: If identity is a story told about a group, then it can be retold; this sense names the telling and the quarrel over it.
senses.whyCN: 如果认同是关于一个群体的故事，那它就能被重讲；这个义项命名讲述本身以及围绕它的争论。

intro.en: Collective joins Latin colligere 'to gather together' (com- 'together' + legere 'to gather, choose') to identity, from Latin idem 'the same'. The compound is modern, shaped by sociology in the twentieth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: collective 由拉丁 colligere「聚集」构成（前缀表「共同」加 legere「收集、挑选」），再与 identity（来自拉丁 idem「同一」）组合。这个复合词是现代的，在二十世纪由社会学塑形。年代均为约数。

items.en: Colligere 'to gather, collect' is com- 'together' plus legere 'to gather, pick, read'. The same verb gives collect, lecture and legend.
items.cn: colligere「聚集、收集」由表示「共同」的前缀加 legere「收集、挑选、读」构成。同一个动词还给出 collect、lecture、legend。

items.en: Idem 'the same' underlies identitas 'sameness', coined in Late Latin as an abstract noun.
items.cn: idem「同一的」是晚期拉丁抽象名词 identitas「同一」的基础。

items.en: Durkheim and his contemporaries described shared representations as a level of social fact, giving the later English phrase its intellectual frame.
items.cn: 涂尔干及其同代人把共享表征描述为一种社会事实层面，为后来英语中的这个词组提供了思想框架。

items.en: Collective identity became a standard term in sociology, political science and history after the 1960s, often in work on nationalism and social movements.
items.cn: 一九六零年代之后，collective identity 成为社会学、政治学与史学的标准术语，常用于民族主义与社会运动研究。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of idem and the precise scholar who first joined the two words are both uncertain; the modern compound has no single coinage date.
items.cn: 来源不确定：idem 更深的来源、以及最早把这两个词并置的学者，均不确定；这个现代复合词没有单一的造词年代。

note.en: Group one separates words built on the same parts; group two holds neighbouring kinds of belonging.
note.cn: 第一组区分由同样构件构成的词；第二组是相邻的归属类型。

entries.definition: Shared by a group; alone it describes ownership or action, with no reference to selfhood.
entries.definitionCN: 由群体共享的；单用时描述所有权或行动，不涉及自我。

entries.definition: A set of objects brought together; it is the product of gathering, not a sense of belonging.
entries.definitionCN: 被聚到一起的一批物件；它是聚集的产物，而非归属感。

entries.definition: The sameness or selfhood of one person or thing; the compound extends it to many.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人或物的同一或自我；复合词把它扩展到许多人。

entries.definition: The belief that group interests should prevail over individual ones; it is a political stance, not a felt identity.
entries.definitionCN: 认为群体利益应高于个人利益的主张；它是政治立场，而非被体验的认同。

entries.definition: Any identity attached to a group; collective identity stresses the shared feeling rather than the category.
entries.definitionCN: 任何附着于群体的身份；集体认同更强调共享感受，而非类别本身。

entries.definition: Identity derived from the social categories one belongs to; it is more analytic and less emotional.
entries.definitionCN: 由所属社会类别得来的身份；更偏分析性，情感色彩更少。

entries.definition: Belonging to a nation; it is one common form of collective identity, not the whole category.
entries.definitionCN: 对民族的归属；它是集体认同的一种常见形式，而非全部。

entries.definition: Mutual support among people with shared interests; it is the action side of collective identity.
entries.definitionCN: 有共同利益者之间的相互支持；它是集体认同的行动一面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin verbs, real sociological terms and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的社会学术语与真实的固定说法。

normal.en: Collect means gather; a collective identity is a 'we' gathered out of many selves.
normal.cn: collect 意为聚集；集体认同就是从许多自我中聚集出来的「我们」。

normal.en: The family runs collect, collection, collective, collectively, collectivism.
normal.cn: 词族包括 collect、collection、collective、collectively、collectivism。

normal.en: A 'we' always implies a 'they': the boundary makes the group visible to itself.
normal.cn: 「我们」总含着「他们」：边界让群体看见自己。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the scale: national collective identity, collective identity and memory, the collapse of collective identity.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出尺度：国家的集体认同、集体认同与记忆、集体认同的瓦解。

normal.en: The plural collective identities fits comparisons among movements, diasporas or firms.
normal.cn: 比较运动、侨居群体或公司时，复数 collective identities 合适。

abstract.en: Picture a photograph that only the people in it can name.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只有照片里的人才叫得出名字的照片。

abstract.en: Picture a rope bridge held up by everyone standing on it at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一座绳桥，靠所有人同时站上去才撑住。

abstract.en: Picture a story that becomes true because enough people agree to keep telling it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个故事，因为足够多的人同意继续讲而变成真的。

examples.en: The museum's exhibit gave the scattered community a visible collective identity.
examples.cn: 博物馆的展览给了这个分散的群体一种看得见的集体认同。

examples.en: War memorials are built to anchor a collective identity in stone.
examples.cn: 战争纪念碑的修建，是为了把集体认同锚定在石头上。

examples.en: Critics warn that a collective identity can silence the differences inside it.
examples.cn: 批评者警告说，集体认同可能压灭它内部的差异。

dict_mnemonic.text: collect（聚在一起）+ identity（同一）＝ 许多人聚成同一个「我们」；记「同一张照片，同一句我们」。

root: collective 源自拉丁 colligere「聚集」，由前缀表「共同」加 legere「收集、挑选」构成，再加形容词后缀；identity 源自晚期拉丁 identitas「同一」，其基础是 idem「同一的」，更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a 'we' from felt belonging to boundary, theory, nation, firm, ethnic community, movement and finally to the argument that all of it is made.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着一个「我们」展开：从被体验的归属，到边界、理论、国家、公司、族群共同体、运动，最后到「这一切都是被建构的」这一论点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many hands holding one photograph and calling the faces in it 'ours'.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多只手共举一张照片，把里面的脸称作「我们的」。

branches.en: FEELING AND FACT: the felt 'we', then the sociological claim that it exists above individuals.
branches.cn: 感受与事实：被体验的「我们」，再是它存在于个体之上的社会学主张。

branches.en: THE EDGE AND THE QUARREL: a boundary defines the group, and the boundary itself can be disputed.
branches.cn: 边界与争论：边界界定群体，而边界本身可以被争夺。

branches.en: THE NATION: schools and ceremonies make a population imagine itself as one body.
branches.cn: 民族国家：学校与仪式让一个人口把自己想象成一个整体。

branches.en: THE FIRM: a company needs a story its staff can share.
branches.cn: 公司：企业需要一个员工可以共享的故事。

branches.en: BELONGING AND CLAIM: ritual keeps a scattered community together, and that 'we' can become a demand.
branches.cn: 归属与主张：仪式让分散的共同体保持一体，而这个「我们」可以变成一项诉求。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin verb of gathering to a Latin noun of sameness; both halves still build common English words.
intro.cn: 这个词组把表示「聚集」的拉丁动词与表示「同一」的拉丁名词结合起来，两半在英语中仍能构成常用词。

latinIntro.en: Latin com- and legere build collective; idem builds identity. No Greek element enters the phrase.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀表「共同」的成分与 legere 构成 collective；idem 构成 identity。这个词组不含希腊成分。

items.example: They collected signatures for the petition.
items.exampleCN: 他们为请愿收集签名。

items.meaning: the act of gathering or the gathered set
items.example: The collection fills three rooms.
items.exampleCN: 这批藏品占满三个房间。

items.example: The land is collective property.
items.exampleCN: 这片土地是集体财产。

items.example: The villagers collectively repaired the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 村民集体修好了桥。

items.meaning: the priority of group over individual
items.example: Collectivism shaped the early commune.
items.exampleCN: 集体主义塑造了早期的公社。

items.example: The collector bought the whole archive.
items.exampleCN: 收藏家买下了整批档案。

items.example: The group's identity survived the move.
items.exampleCN: 群体的认同在迁移后存活下来。

items.example: Members identify with the old songs.
items.exampleCN: 成员们认同那些老歌。

definition_zh: 社会身份；由所属群体与类别得来的身份；社会认同理论中「我们—他们」分类产生的自我概念
definition_en: the part of a person's self-concept that comes from the social groups and categories they belong to
core_image: 更衣室里两排柜子，一排挂着工装，一排挂着西装，同一个人在两排之间换衣服
scene: 她从车间调到讲台，工装换成西装，旧同事看她的眼神也跟着变了。Her social identity shifted with the move from the factory floor to the lecture hall.
sceneCN: 这里 social identity 指由所属群体与职业类别得来的身份（第 1 个义项：由群体归属构成的身份）；句意为她的社会身份随着从车间到讲台的变动而改变。

pos.zh: 社会身份；社会认同（可数，指一种身份；不可数，指这一概念）

derivatives.zh: 社会的；社交的（由拉丁 socialis 经法语进入，词根 socius 意为「同伴」，是本词组的形容词基础）
在社会上；社交上（由基础形容词加表方式的副词后缀而来，由性质转指方式）
社会；社团（经法语 societe 来自拉丁 societas「伙伴关系」，由「同伴」转指「共同生活的人群」）
使社会化；社交（由基础形容词加表使成过程的动词后缀而来，由性质转指使之形成的过程）
社会化（由基础动词加表过程或结果的名词后缀而来，由动作转指过程）

senses.title: Identity from membership
senses.titleCN: 由群体归属构成的身份
senses.definition: the self-description a person draws from the groups they belong to
senses.definitionCN: 一个人从所属群体中得出的自我描述
senses.example: Being a nurse gave her a social identity that outlasted the job.
senses.exampleCN: 当护士给了她一种比这份工作更持久的社会身份。
senses.why: Social marks where the identity comes from: not the private self but the categories a person shares with others.
senses.whyCN: 前一个成分标出身份的来源：不是私人的自我，而是与他人共享的类别。

senses.title: The theory of in-group and out-group
senses.definition: Tajfel and Turner's account of how categorising people into 'us' and 'them' shapes self-esteem and bias
senses.definitionCN: 泰弗尔与特纳的解释：把人分成「我们」与「他们」如何塑造自尊与偏见
senses.example: Social identity theory predicts that fans will defend their own group first.
senses.exampleCN: 社会认同理论预测，球迷会先维护自己所属的群体。
senses.why: The phrase became a named theory in the 1970s; this sense is the technical, testable version of the everyday one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组在一九七零年代成为有名有姓的理论；这个义项是日常义项的技术化、可检验版本。

senses.title: Role identity
senses.definition: the identity attached to a social role such as parent, student or soldier
senses.definitionCN: 附着于社会角色（如父母、学生、士兵）的身份
senses.example: Her social identity as a mother reorganised her working hours.
senses.exampleCN: 作为母亲的社会身份重新安排了她的工作时间。
senses.why: Roles are scripts others expect; taking one up gives a person a recognised place in a group.
senses.whyCN: 角色是他人期待的一套脚本；承担一个角色，就给了个人一个被承认的位置。

senses.title: Class and status
senses.definition: the identity derived from economic position, education and the respect others accord
senses.definitionCN: 由经济位置、教育与他人给予的尊重得来的身份
senses.example: His accent still marked his social identity at the university.
senses.exampleCN: 在大学里，他的口音仍然标出他的社会身份。
senses.why: Class is read from small signs; identity here is the rank a person is placed in by others.
senses.whyCN: 阶层从小迹象里被读出；这里的身份是他人把人放进去的等级。

senses.title: Professional identity
senses.definition: the shared norms, language and pride that come with belonging to a profession
senses.definitionCN: 属于一个职业所带来的共享规范、语言与自豪感
senses.example: Medical school builds a professional social identity as much as a skill set.
senses.exampleCN: 医学院既培养技能，也塑造一种职业性的社会身份。
senses.why: A profession trains its members to see like one another; the identity is the shared way of looking.
senses.whyCN: 一个职业训练成员以相同方式看世界；这种身份就是共享的看世界的方式。

senses.title: Stigmatised identity
senses.definition: an identity that others treat as a mark of lesser value, often forcing management of appearance
senses.definitionCN: 被他人视为低价值标记的身份，常迫使当事人管理自己的外在表现
senses.example: Goffman showed how a stigmatised social identity is managed in daily talk.
senses.exampleCN: 戈夫曼展示了被污名化的社会身份如何在日常言谈中被管理。
senses.why: Identity is not only claimed but assigned; when the assignment is negative, the phrase describes a burden.
senses.whyCN: 身份不只是被主张，也被指派；当指派是负面的，这个词组描述的就是一种负担。

senses.title: Identity presented online
senses.definition: the version of social identity a person selects and performs on platforms and profiles
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在平台与个人资料上选择并表演的那版社会身份
senses.example: Online, her social identity was edited into a cleaner, happier story.
senses.exampleCN: 在线上，她的社会身份被编辑成一个更干净、更快乐的故事。
senses.why: When audiences can be chosen, identity becomes a performance with settings and filters.
senses.whyCN: 当受众可以被挑选，身份就变成一场带设置与滤镜的表演。

senses.title: Salience and activation
senses.definition: the degree to which one membership becomes the identity a person acts on in a given situation
senses.definitionCN: 在特定情境中，某一归属成为当事人据以行动的身份的程度
senses.example: At the border, her national social identity became suddenly salient.
senses.exampleCN: 在边境，她的国家社会身份突然变得显著。
senses.why: People hold many memberships at once; the one that is switched on depends on the setting, not on a fixed hierarchy.
senses.whyCN: 人同时拥有许多归属；被打开的那一个取决于情境，而非固定的等级。

intro.en: Social comes from Latin socialis 'of companions', from socius 'companion, ally'. Identity comes from Latin idem 'the same'. The theory that made the phrase famous was published by Tajfel and Turner in the 1970s. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: social 来自拉丁 socialis「同伴的」，词根 socius「同伴、盟友」。identity 来自拉丁 idem「同一的」。使这个词组成名的理论由泰弗尔与特纳在一九七零年代发表。年代均为约数。

items.en: Socius meant 'companion, ally, associate'. A link with a root meaning 'to follow' has been suggested, but it remains a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、盟友、合伙人」。有人提出它与一个意为「跟随」的词根有关，但那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Socialis 'of a companion or alliance' gave French social and English social, widening from personal companionship to organised society.
