items.cn: socialis「同伴的、结盟的」给出法语 social 与英语 social，词义从私人交往扩展到有组织的社会。

items.en: Idem 'the same' underlies identitas, the Late Latin abstract noun that English identity descends from.
items.cn: idem「同一的」是晚期拉丁抽象名词 identitas 的基础，英语 identity 即由此而来。

items.en: Tajfel's experiments on group bias in the 1970s, developed with Turner, produced social identity theory: memberships shape self-concept through comparison with out-groups.
items.cn: 泰弗尔在一九七零年代关于群体偏见的实验，与特纳共同发展为社会认同理论：归属通过对内群外群的比较塑造自我概念。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of socius is unresolved, and the attribution of the theory to one date or paper oversimplifies a decade of collaborative work.
items.cn: 来源不确定：socius 在拉丁语之前的来源未有定论；把该理论系于某一日期或某一篇论文，也简化了十年间的合作研究。

note.en: Group one separates the social family; group two holds neighbouring identity terms.
note.cn: 第一组区分 social 词族；第二组是相邻的身份术语。

entries.definition: Of society or companionship; alone it can describe a party, an insect or a policy.
entries.definitionCN: 关于社会或交往的；单用时可以形容聚会、昆虫或政策。

entries.definition: An organised community; the identity belongs to a person, the society is the collectivity.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的共同体；身份属于个人，社会则是集合体。

entries.definition: Fond of company; the suffix turns the root toward personality, not identity.
entries.definitionCN: 喜欢与人相处的；后缀把词根转向性格，而非身份。

entries.definition: A political-economic system; it is a programme, not a personal membership.
entries.definitionCN: 一种政治经济制度；它是纲领，而非个人归属。

entries.definition: The group's shared sense of itself; social identity is the individual's side of the same coin.
entries.definitionCN: 群体对自身的共享感受；社会身份是同一枚硬币的个人一面。

entries.definition: Everything a person believes about themselves; social identity is one component of it.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人关于自己的全部看法；社会身份是其中的一个成分。

entries.definition: The prestige attached to a position; identity is the felt membership, status is its ranking.
entries.definitionCN: 附着于某个位置的声望；身份是被体验的归属，地位是它的排序。

entries.definition: The expected behaviour attached to a position; a role can supply an identity but is not identical with it.
entries.definitionCN: 附着于某个位置的预期行为；角色可以提供身份，但不等于身份。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin roots, real theory names and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的理论名称与真实的固定说法。

normal.en: Social points to a companion; social identity is the self you get from companions.
normal.cn: social 指向同伴；社会身份就是从同伴那里得到的自我。

normal.en: The same identitas family gives identify, identification and identical.
normal.cn: 同一个 identitas 词族给出 identify、identification、identical。

normal.en: Tajfel and Turner made the phrase a theory: categorise, compare, then favour your own group.
normal.cn: 泰弗尔与特纳把这个词组变成理论：分类、比较，然后偏袒自己所属的群体。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the research field: social identity theory, social identity threat, multiple social identities.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出研究领域：社会认同理论、社会认同威胁、多重社会身份。

normal.en: The plural social identities fits a person who holds several memberships at once.
normal.cn: 指一个人同时拥有多种归属时，复数 social identities 合适。

abstract.en: Picture a wardrobe with two rows of clothes, and one person changing between them.
abstract.cn: 想象一个衣橱，两排衣服，同一个人在两排之间更换。

abstract.en: Picture a badge that is invisible to its wearer but bright to everyone else.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚佩戴者看不见、旁人却看得很亮的徽章。

abstract.en: Picture a switchboard where only one membership light is on at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一块配电盘，同一时刻只有一盏归属的灯亮着。

examples.en: Sport clubs give migrants a social identity before they learn the language.
examples.cn: 体育俱乐部在移民学会当地语言之前，先给了他们一种社会身份。

examples.en: Social identity theory explains why a insult to one member feels like an insult to all.
examples.cn: 社会认同理论解释了为什么对一名成员的侮辱会被当作对全体的侮辱。

examples.en: Remote work weakened the professional social identity of the junior staff.
examples.cn: 远程工作削弱了年轻员工的职业社会身份。

dict_mnemonic.text: social（同伴的）+ identity（同一）＝ 你与同伴共享的那部分「我是谁」；记「换衣服，也换别人看你的眼光」。

root: social 源自拉丁 socialis「同伴的」，词根 socius 意为「同伴、盟友」，更早来源不确定；identity 源自晚期拉丁 identitas「同一」，由 idem「同一的」构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from membership through theory, role, class, profession, stigma and online performance to the switching on of one identity in a situation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从群体归属出发，经理论、角色、阶层、职业、污名与线上表演，直到某一身份在具体情境中被打开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rows of clothes in one wardrobe, and one person moving between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个衣橱里的两排衣服，同一个人在两排之间走动。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY AND THE THEORY: belonging first, then the model of us-and-them that explains it.
branches.cn: 日常与理论：先是归属，再是解释归属的「我们与他们」模型。

branches.en: THE SCRIPT: a role supplies a recognised place and its expected behaviour.
branches.cn: 脚本：角色提供一个被承认的位置及其预期行为。

branches.en: THE RANK: class is read from signs and assigned by others.
branches.cn: 等级：阶层从小迹象里被读出，并由他人指派。

branches.en: THE PROFESSION: training installs a shared way of seeing.
branches.cn: 职业：训练装进一套共享的看世界的方式。

branches.en: ASSIGNED, PERFORMED, SWITCHED ON: stigma imposed from outside, identity edited online, and one membership made salient.
branches.cn: 被指派、被表演、被打开：外部强加的污名，线上编辑的身份，以及被激活的某一归属。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin adjective of companionship to a Latin noun of sameness; both halves are still productive in English.
intro.cn: 这个词组把表示「同伴关系」的拉丁形容词与表示「同一」的拉丁名词结合起来，两半在英语中仍有构词能力。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius and socialis supply the first element; idem and identitas supply the second. No Greek element is present.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius 与 socialis 提供前一成分；idem 与 identitas 提供后一成分。这个词组不含希腊成分。

items.example: Social rules differ between cultures.
items.exampleCN: 社会规则在不同文化间有差异。

items.example: The district is socially mixed.
items.exampleCN: 这个区在社会构成上是混杂的。

items.example: Society changed faster than the law.
items.exampleCN: 社会的变化快于法律。

items.meaningCN: 好交际的；喜欢与人相处的
items.example: He is sociable at work but silent at home.
items.exampleCN: 他在单位很合群，在家却沉默。

items.meaning: to mix with others; to fit to society
items.example: Children socialize through play.
items.exampleCN: 儿童通过游戏社会化。

items.meaning: the process of learning a society's ways
items.example: Language is central to socialization.
items.exampleCN: 语言在社会化中处于核心位置。

items.example: Identity is partly chosen and partly assigned.
items.exampleCN: 身份一部分是被选择的，一部分是被指派的。

items.meaning: to recognise or declare oneself as belonging
items.example: Many readers identify with the narrator.
items.exampleCN: 许多读者认同叙述者。

definition_zh: 族群性；族群身份；族裔出身；（人口统计中的）族群类别
definition_en: the quality of belonging to a people defined by shared ancestry, language or culture
core_image: 一张登记表上并列着「语言」「出生地」「族群」三栏，填表人的笔在三栏之间来回移动
scene: 登记表先问语言，再问出生地，最后才问族群，填表的人在三栏之间犹豫了很久。The census form asked for ethnicity before it asked for language.
sceneCN: 这里 ethnicity 指登记表中的族群类别（第 7 个义项：统计类别）；句意为普查表在问语言之前先问了族群。

pos.zh: 族群性；族群身份（不可数，指这种属性；可数时指某一具体族群归属）
（统计）族群类别（可数）

derivatives.zh: 族群的；族裔的（由希腊 ethnikos 经拉丁进入，由「民族的」转指「属于某一族群的」）
按族群地；在族裔方面（由基础形容词加表方面的副词后缀而来，由性质转指方面）
民族学（由表族群的前缀加表学科的名词后缀而来，由「族群」转指「对族群的研究」）
民族志（由表族群的前缀加表记述的名词后缀而来，由「族群」转指「对族群的书写描述」）
族群中心主义的（由表族群的前缀加表中心的成分而来，由「族群」转指「以本族为中心」）

senses.title: Ethnic quality
senses.definition: the condition of belonging to a people with shared ancestry and culture
senses.definitionCN: 属于一个共享祖先与文化的民族的状态
senses.example: Her ethnicity was never a single box on any form.
senses.exampleCN: 在任何表格上，她的族群属性从来都不止一个框。
senses.why: The suffix names a quality, not a person: ethnicity is the property of belonging, abstracted from any one group.
senses.whyCN: 这个词尾命名一种性质，而不是一个人：该词表示归属的属性，从任何具体群体中抽象出来。

senses.title: An ethnic group itself
senses.definition: a named people or community distinguished by ancestry, language or custom
senses.definitionCN: 以祖先、语言或习俗相区分的一个有名称的民族或共同体
senses.example: Three ethnicities share the same mountain valley.
senses.exampleCN: 三个族群共处同一条山谷。
senses.why: Abstract nouns often turn countable: one can speak of several ethnicities as several named peoples.
senses.whyCN: 抽象名词常转为可数：人们可以把若干族群说成若干有名称的民族。

senses.title: Ethnic background
senses.definition: the ancestry a person reports when asked where their family came from
senses.definitionCN: 被问及家族来历时，一个人所报告的祖先来源
senses.example: The job form asked for ethnicity but not for religion.
senses.exampleCN: 求职表问了族裔出身，却没问宗教。
senses.why: Institutions need a short answer about origin, so ethnicity becomes a self-reported background.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要一个关于来源的简短回答，于是族群性变成自我报告的出身。

senses.title: Cultural markers
senses.definition: the language, food, dress and ritual by which an ethnic boundary is made visible
senses.definitionCN: 使族群边界变得可见的语言、饮食、服饰与仪式
senses.example: Ethnicity was performed at the wedding through song and dress.
senses.exampleCN: 在婚礼上，族群性通过歌声与服饰被表演出来。
senses.why: Boundaries need signs; culture supplies the visible markers that let people read who belongs.
senses.whyCN: 边界需要标记；文化提供可见的符号，让人读出谁属于其中。

senses.title: Ascribed or chosen
senses.definition: the degree to which ethnic membership is imposed by others or claimed by the person
senses.definitionCN: 族群归属在多大程度上由他人强加，或由本人主张
senses.example: His ethnicity was assigned by a clerk who never asked him.
senses.exampleCN: 他的族群身份是由一名从未问过他的办事员指派的。
senses.why: Ethnicity sits between inheritance and assertion: one can be counted in a group one does not claim.
senses.whyCN: 族群性处在继承与主张之间：一个人可能被计入一个自己并不主张的群体。

senses.title: Political ethnicity
senses.definition: ethnic belonging organised into a claim for power, territory or recognition
senses.definitionCN: 把族群归属组织成对权力、领土或承认的主张
senses.example: Ethnicity became a voting bloc in the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 在首都，族群性变成了一个投票集团。
senses.why: When leaders speak for a group, a cultural boundary hardens into a political constituency.
senses.whyCN: 当领袖代表一个群体发言，文化边界就硬化为政治选区。

senses.title: A statistical category
senses.definition: a fixed set of boxes used by censuses and surveys to count populations
senses.definitionCN: 普查与调查用来清点人口的一套固定选项
senses.example: The census added a new ethnicity category that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年普查新增了一个族群类别。
senses.why: Counting requires flat labels, so a fluid identity is frozen into a list of options.
senses.whyCN: 清点需要扁平的标签，于是流动的身份被冻结成一列选项。

senses.title: Ethnicity versus race
senses.definition: the analytic distinction between cultural belonging and categories built on physical descent
senses.definitionCN: 文化归属与基于身体世系的类别之间的分析性区别
senses.example: The seminar treated ethnicity and race as related but not interchangeable.
senses.exampleCN: 研讨班把族群性与种族视为相关但不可互换的概念。
senses.why: Both classify people, but ethnicity stresses culture and ancestry while race stresses descent as socially read from bodies.
senses.whyCN: 两者都对人群分类，但族群性强调文化与祖先，种族则强调从身体上被社会读出的世系。

intro.en: Ethnicity is built on Greek ethnos 'nation, people', through ethnikos and Latin ethnicus, with the abstract ending -ity. The English noun is a modern formation. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ethnicity 建立在希腊 ethnos「民族、人群」之上，经 ethnikos 与拉丁 ethnicus，再加抽象词尾 -ity。这个英语名词是现代的构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ethnos meant 'a people, nation, tribe, band'. Its own origin is uncertain; the old suggestion of a link with ethos 'custom' is a hypothesis, not an established derivation.
items.cn: ethnos 意为「人群、民族、部落、队伍」。它自身的来源不确定；旧时把它与 ethos「习俗」联系起来的说法只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Ethnikos meant 'of a nation or people'. In Jewish and early Christian Greek, ta ethne 'the nations' came to mean the Gentiles, those outside the covenant.
items.cn: ethnikos 意为「民族的、人群的」。在犹太与早期基督教希腊语中，ta ethne「诸民族」转指外邦人，即盟约之外的人。

items.en: Latin ethnicus was borrowed from Greek and used for 'heathen, pagan'; English ethnic entered through this channel with the same religious sense.
items.cn: 拉丁 ethnicus 借自希腊语，用来指「异教的、外邦的」；英语 ethnic 经这条通道进入，也带着同样的宗教含义。

items.en: The abstract noun ethnicity appears in the nineteenth century and becomes common in the twentieth, as anthropology and censuses needed a word for cultural belonging distinct from race.
items.cn: 抽象名词 ethnicity 在十九世纪出现，到二十世纪变得常用，因为人类学与普查需要一个区别于种族的词来表示文化归属。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Greek origin of ethnos is unresolved, and the exact coinage date of the English noun is not fixed; nineteenth-century uses are occasional rather than systematic.
items.cn: 来源不确定：ethnos 在希腊语之前的来源未有定论；这个英语名词的确切造词年代也不固定，十九世纪的用法是零星的，而非系统性的。

note.en: Group one separates the ethnic family; group two holds terms that classify people.
note.cn: 第一组区分 ethnic 词族；第二组是对人进行分类的术语。

entries.definition: Of a people or group; the adjective describes, while ethnicity names the property or category.
entries.definitionCN: 族群的；某个民族的。形容词作描述，而 ethnicity 命名属性或类别。

entries.definition: A principle of conduct, from Greek ethos 'custom'; it looks almost identical but belongs to moral philosophy.
entries.definitionCN: 行为原则，来自希腊 ethos「习俗」；拼写几乎相同，却属于道德哲学。

entries.definition: The study of moral principles; the plural is a discipline, not a group of people.
entries.definitionCN: 对道德原则的研究；复数形式指一门学科，而非一群人。

entries.definition: The comparative study of peoples; the suffix marks a discipline rather than a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 对各民族的比较研究；后缀标记学科，而非性质。

entries.definition: A category built on descent and physical traits as socially read; ethnicity stresses culture and ancestry instead.
entries.definitionCN: 基于世系与被社会解读的身体特征的类别；族群性则强调文化与祖先。

entries.definition: Legal citizenship of a state; it is a passport fact, not a cultural belonging.
entries.definitionCN: 对某个国家的法定公民身份；它是护照上的事实，而非文化归属。

entries.definition: A smaller kin-based people; it is one possible ethnic unit, often with a colonial history of labelling.
entries.definitionCN: 较小的以亲属为基础的人群；它是族群的一种可能单位，常带有殖民标签的历史。

entries.definition: The traditions and objects passed down; ethnicity is the belonging, heritage is the content handed over.
entries.definitionCN: 传下来的传统与物件；族群性是归属，遗产是被交下的内容。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek forms, real modern usage and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语形式、真实的现代用法与真实的固定说法。

normal.en: Ethnos meant a people; ethnicity is the abstract name of belonging to one.
normal.cn: ethnos 指一群人；ethnicity 是归属于其中之一的抽象名称。

normal.en: Keep ethnic and ethic apart by the last letters: one has n for nation, the other has no n.
normal.cn: 靠末尾字母区分 ethnic 与 ethic：一个有 n，联想到 nation；一个没有。

normal.en: The old religious sense survives in the history: the nations outside the covenant were called the ethne.
normal.cn: 旧的宗教含义留在历史里：盟约之外的人群曾被称为 ethne。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: ethnicity and race, ethnicity data, a sense of ethnicity.
normal.cn: 固定说法划出领域：族群与种族、族群数据、族群意识。

normal.en: The plural ethnicities counts named peoples or reported categories.
normal.cn: 复数 ethnicities 用来数有名称的族群或登记的类别。

abstract.en: Picture a form with three boxes, where the pen hesitates because the boxes do not match the family.
abstract.cn: 想象一张有三个框的表格，笔在框上犹豫，因为框与家族并不吻合。

abstract.en: Picture a boundary drawn in language, food and song rather than in ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一道边界，用语言、饮食与歌声画出，而不是用墨水。

abstract.en: Picture a label that can be worn, refused, or pinned on someone by a clerk.
abstract.cn: 想象一个标签，可以被佩戴、拒绝，或被办事员别到别人身上。

examples.en: Anthropologists stopped treating ethnicity as a fixed biological fact.
examples.cn: 人类学者不再把族群性当作固定的生物学事实。

examples.en: The school records ethnicity only to check that services reach every group.
examples.cn: 学校登记族群身份，只为核查服务是否覆盖每个群体。

examples.en: Her ethnicity shaped the food she cooked but not the language she wrote in.
examples.cn: 她的族群性塑造了她做的菜，却没有决定她写作所用的语言。

dict_mnemonic.text: ethnos（人群）+ ity（性质）＝ 属于某一群人的那种性质；记「表格上的一个框，饭桌上的一桌菜」。

root: 源自希腊 ethnos「人群、民族」，其更早来源不确定；经形容词 ethnikos 与拉丁 ethnicus 传入欧洲语言，再加抽象名词后缀构成英语名词，属现代学术构词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the abstract property of belonging to a named people, then to reported ancestry, cultural markers, attribution, politics, statistics and the contrast with race.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从归属的抽象属性，移到有名称的族群，再到自我报告的出身、文化标记、归属指派、政治化、统计类别，以及与种族的对照。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a form with three boxes, and a pen that hesitates between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张有三个框的表格，一支笔在框间犹豫。

branches.en: PROPERTY AND REPORT: belonging as an abstract quality, then as the ancestry a person states.
branches.cn: 属性与申报：先是作为抽象性质的归属，再是个人陈述的祖先来源。

branches.en: A NAMED PEOPLE: the abstract noun turns countable when several peoples are meant.
branches.cn: 有名称的人群：当指若干民族时，抽象名词转为可数。

branches.en: SIGNS AND ASSIGNMENT: culture makes the boundary visible, and others may pin the label on.
branches.cn: 标记与指派：文化让边界可见，他人也可能把标签别上来。

branches.en: THE VOTE: a cultural boundary hardens into a political claim.
branches.cn: 选票：文化边界硬化为政治主张。

branches.en: THE BOX AND THE CONTRAST: statistics freeze the category, and analysis separates it from race.
branches.cn: 表格与对照：统计冻结类别，分析则把它与种族分开。

intro.en: Ethnicity is a Greek-derived base with a Latin abstract ending; the same base builds a large learned family.
intro.cn: ethnicity 是希腊来源的词干加拉丁抽象词尾；同一词干构成一个很大的学术词族。

latinIntro.en: The base is Greek ethnos, transmitted through Latin ethnicus; the ending -ity is Latin -itas. The word is a modern learned formation rather than a classical one.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是希腊 ethnos，经拉丁 ethnicus 传来；词尾 -ity 来自拉丁 -itas。这个词是现代的学术构成，而非古典词。

items.example: The city has many ethnic neighbourhoods.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市有许多族群社区。

items.example: The district is ethnically mixed.
items.exampleCN: 这个区在族群上是混合的。

items.meaningCN: 民族学；对各民族的比较研究
items.example: Ethnology compares kinship systems.
items.exampleCN: 民族学比较亲属制度。

items.meaning: the description of a people by fieldwork
items.meaningCN: 民族志；通过田野调查对某群体的描述
items.example: Her ethnography of the village took two years.
items.exampleCN: 她对那个村庄的民族志研究花了两年。

items.meaning: judging others by one's own group's standards
items.meaningCN: 族群中心主义的；以本族标准评判他人
items.example: The old textbook was openly ethnocentric.
items.exampleCN: 那本旧教科书公开带有族群中心主义。

items.meaning: the habit of centring one's own people
items.example: Ethnocentrism distorts the record of encounters.
items.exampleCN: 族群中心主义会扭曲相遇的记录。

items.example: The map shows ethnolinguistic boundaries.
items.exampleCN: 地图显示了族群语言的边界。

items.meaning: a named people within a larger population
items.meaningCN: 较大人口中的一个有名称族群
items.example: Each ethnic group kept its own songs.
items.exampleCN: 每个族群都保留了自己的歌。

definition_zh: 族群的；族裔的；具有族群特色的；（旧义）异教的、外邦的
definition_en: relating to a people that shares ancestry, language or culture, especially one within a larger society
core_image: 一条街上并排挂着不同文字的招牌，同一座城市里各有各的节日与菜市场
scene: 街角的小店卖着别处的香料，收音机里放着同一种语言的歌。The shop sells ethnic food and plays music from the same region.
sceneCN: 这里 ethnic 指具有族群特色的（第 3 个义项：文化上可辨识的族群风格）；句意为这家店卖族群风味的食物，放同一地区的音乐。

pos.zh: 族群的；族裔的（指与某一共享祖先或文化的群体有关）
具有族群特色的（常指食物、音乐、服饰等文化标记）
（旧用法，今多含冒犯意味）少数族裔成员

collocations.zh: 华裔；族裔意义上的华人

derivatives.zh: 族群性；族群身份（由基础形容词加表抽象属性的名词后缀而来，由形容词转指抽象属性）
在族群方面（由基础形容词加表方面的副词后缀而来，由形容词转指方面）
族群……（希腊词干进入复合词，如民族学、民族志，由「人群」转指研究或描述的对象）
族群中心主义的（由表族群的前缀加表中心的成分而来，由「族群」转指「以本族为中心」）

senses.title: Of a people
senses.definition: relating to a people that shares ancestry, language and custom
senses.definitionCN: 与一个共享祖先、语言与习俗的人群有关的
senses.example: The region has three ethnic languages and one official one.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区有三种族群语言和一种官方语言。
senses.why: The Greek base names a people; the adjective simply marks that relation before any question of size or power.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词干命名一群人；这个形容词只是标记那种关系，尚不涉及人数或权力。

senses.title: Of a minority within a state
senses.definition: relating to a group distinguished from the national majority, often by origin
senses.definitionCN: 与一个因来源等原因区别于国家多数群体的群体有关的
senses.example: Ethnic minorities won the right to teach in their own language.
senses.exampleCN: 少数族裔赢得了用本族语言教学的权利。
senses.why: Once a state has a majority, the adjective usually marks the smaller group; the word acquires a political asymmetry.
senses.whyCN: 一旦国家有了多数群体，这个形容词通常标记较小的群体；词义由此带上政治上的不对称。

senses.title: Culturally distinctive
senses.definition: markedly characteristic of a particular people, especially in food, music or dress
senses.definitionCN: 明显带有某一人群特征的，尤指饮食、音乐或服饰
senses.example: The festival turned the square into an ethnic market for a weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 节日把广场变成了一个为期两天的族群集市。
senses.why: Culture is visible; the adjective can describe the signs themselves, not only the people who carry them.
senses.whyCN: 文化是可见的；这个形容词可以描述那些标记本身，而不只是携带标记的人。

senses.title: Defined within a state
senses.titleCN: 在国家内部按族群界定
senses.definition: used to specify a community by ethnicity when a broader national label would be ambiguous
senses.definitionCN: 当更宽的国家标签会造成歧义时，用族群来限定某一群体
senses.example: The report distinguishes ethnic Albanians from Albanian citizens.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把族裔上的阿尔巴尼亚人与阿尔巴尼亚公民区分开来。
senses.why: A passport and a people do not coincide; the adjective lets a writer separate the two.
senses.whyCN: 护照与人群并不重合；这个形容词让作者把两者分开。

senses.title: Heathen or Gentile
senses.definition: the older religious sense: belonging to the peoples outside a covenant faith
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的宗教含义：属于盟约信仰之外的人群
senses.example: The old translation used ethnic for those outside the faith.
senses.exampleCN: 旧译本用这个词指信仰之外的人。
senses.why: The word entered English through Latin with this sense; it survives mainly in historical writing about religious language.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经拉丁语进入英语时就带着这个含义；如今主要存活在关于宗教语言的历史写作中。

senses.title: Marking identity
senses.definition: used of the signs, names and practices through which ethnic membership is recognised
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示据以辨认族群归属的标志、名称与做法
senses.example: Ethnic names on the map were replaced by colonial ones.
senses.exampleCN: 地图上的族群地名被殖民地名取代。
senses.why: Identity needs markers; the adjective attaches to the markers as much as to the people.
senses.whyCN: 认同需要标记；这个形容词既附着于人，也附着于标记。

senses.title: The dated noun
senses.definition: a now dated and often offensive noun for a member of a minority group
senses.definitionCN: 现已过时、且常含冒犯意味的用法，指少数群体的成员
senses.example: The novel's use of the noun now reads as a period insult.
senses.exampleCN: 小说里那个名词的用法，如今读来是那个时代的侮辱。
senses.why: When a label names people rather than relations, it turns them into a category; modern usage avoids it for that reason.
senses.whyCN: 当标签命名的是人而不是关系，它就把人变成一个类别；现代用法因此避免它。

senses.title: Framing conflict
senses.definition: used to describe violence or tension presented as occurring between ethnic groups
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述被呈现为发生在族群之间的暴力或紧张
senses.example: The phrase ethnic conflict hides how many motives were economic.
senses.exampleCN: 「族群冲突」这一说法掩盖了多少经济动机。
senses.why: Naming a war 'ethnic' is itself an interpretation; this sense names the framing rather than the fact.
senses.whyCN: 把一场战争称作「族群的」本身就是一种解释；这个义项命名的是框定方式，而非事实。

intro.en: Ethnic comes from Greek ethnikos 'of a people', from ethnos 'nation, people', through Latin ethnicus 'heathen'. The modern social sense is a later English development. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ethnic 来自希腊 ethnikos「民族的」，词根 ethnos「民族、人群」，经拉丁 ethnicus「异教的」进入。现代的社会学含义是英语后来发展出的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ethnos meant 'people, nation, tribe'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; a link with ethos 'custom' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: ethnos 意为「人群、民族、部落」。它更深的来源不确定；与 ethos「习俗」的联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Ethnikos 'of a people' was used in Jewish and Christian Greek for the nations outside the faith, ta ethne, hence 'Gentile'.
items.cn: ethnikos「民族的」在犹太与基督教希腊语中用来指信仰之外的诸民族 ta ethne，因而带上「外邦人」义。

items.en: Latin ethnicus 'heathen, pagan' carried the religious sense into European languages.
items.cn: 拉丁 ethnicus「异教的、外邦的」把宗教含义带入欧洲各语言。

items.en: English ethnic first appears with the religious sense, then shifts in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries toward peoples and their cultures.
items.cn: 英语 ethnic 最初带宗教含义，十九、二十世纪转向指人群及其文化。

items.en: After the mid-twentieth century the adjective commonly marks minorities, cultural style and identity, and the noun became dated and offensive.
items.cn: 二十世纪中叶以后，这个形容词常标记少数群体、文化风格与认同，其名词形式则变得过时且含冒犯意味。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Greek origin of ethnos is unresolved, and the precise century in which the social sense became dominant varies by source.
items.cn: 来源不确定：ethnos 在希腊语之前的来源未有定论；社会义成为主流的精确年代，各资料说法不一。

note.en: Group one is the classic one-letter confusion; group two holds terms for kinds of group and belonging.
note.cn: 第一组是最典型的差一个字母的混淆；第二组是群体与归属类型的术语。

entries.definition: A principle of conduct, from Greek ethos 'custom'. It shares the first four letters but belongs to moral philosophy.
entries.definitionCN: 行为原则，来自希腊 ethos「习俗」。前四个字母相同，却属于道德哲学。

entries.definition: The study of moral principles; it is a field of inquiry, not a people.
entries.definitionCN: 对道德原则的研究；它是一门探究领域，而非一群人。

entries.definition: The abstract property or category; the adjective describes and the noun names.
entries.definitionCN: 抽象的属性或类别；形容词作描述，名词作命名。

entries.definition: An older adjective variant now largely replaced by ethnic; it appears mostly in nineteenth-century texts.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的形容词变体，今多被 ethnic 取代；主要见于十九世纪文本。

entries.definition: Relating to categories built on descent and physical traits; ethnic stresses culture and ancestry rather than bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 与基于世系和身体特征的类别有关的；ethnic 强调文化与祖先，而非身体。

entries.definition: Relating to a state or a whole nation; it is a political frame, not a minority frame.
entries.definitionCN: 与国家或整个民族有关的；它是政治框架，而非少数群体框架。

entries.definition: Relating to shared ways of life; ethnic adds the sense of a bounded people and its ancestry.
entries.definitionCN: 与共享生活方式有关的；ethnic 另加「有边界的人群及其祖先」之意。

entries.definition: Relating to a tribe; it is narrower and often carries a colonial tone.
entries.definitionCN: 与部落有关的；范围更窄，且常带殖民语气。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek forms, real collocations and real usage history.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语形式、真实搭配与真实的用法史。

normal.en: Ethnic has n for nation; ethic has no n and belongs to morals.
normal.cn: ethnic 有 n，联想到 nation；ethic 没有 n，属于道德。

normal.en: The root ethnos is a people, so the adjective always points at a group before it points at a trait.
normal.cn: 词根 ethnos 是一群人，所以这个形容词先指向群体，再指向特征。

normal.en: The religious sense came first in English: ethnic meant outside the faith before it meant inside a minority.
normal.cn: 英语里宗教含义先到：ethnic 先指信仰之外，后指少数群体之内。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the modern field: ethnic group, ethnic minority, ethnic food, ethnic conflict.
normal.cn: 固定说法划出现代领域：族群、少数族裔、族群风味食物、族群冲突。

normal.en: The noun ethnics is dated and offensive; modern writing uses the adjective only.
normal.cn: 名词 ethnics 已过时且含冒犯意味；现代写作只用形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a street where every shop window writes a different script.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街，每扇橱窗写着不同的文字。

abstract.en: Picture a label that describes a relation until someone turns it into a name for a person.
abstract.cn: 想象一个标签，本来描述关系，直到有人把它变成对人的称呼。

abstract.en: Picture a map with two layers of names, one printed over the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图有两层地名，一层印在另一层上。

examples.en: Ethnic diversity is written into the city's street names.
examples.cn: 族群多样性写在这座城市的街道名里。

examples.en: The law protects ethnic minorities without creating separate courts.
examples.cn: 法律保护少数族裔，却不另设独立法庭。

examples.en: Journalists should ask who benefits from calling a dispute ethnic.
examples.cn: 记者应当追问，把一场争端称为族群冲突对谁有利。

dict_mnemonic.text: ethnos（人群）+ ic（……的）＝ 属于某一人群的；记「有 n 就是 nation，没 n 就是 moral」。

root: 源自希腊 ethnos「人群、民族」，更早来源不确定；经形容词 ethnikos「民族的、外邦的」与拉丁 ethnicus「异教的」进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a neutral relation to a people, to minority status, cultural style, state-internal specification, the old religious sense, identity markers, the dated noun and the framing of conflict.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从与人群的中性关系，移到少数地位、文化风格、国家内部的限定、旧宗教义、认同标记、过时名词，以及冲突的框定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one street, many scripts, and a majority that decides which script is official.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条街，多种文字，以及决定哪种文字官方的多数群体。

branches.en: NEUTRAL AND ASYMMETRIC: a people in general, then a smaller people inside a state.
branches.cn: 中性与不对称：先是一般的人群，再是国家之内较小的人群。

branches.en: VISIBLE SIGNS: food, music and names make the relation readable.
branches.cn: 可见标记：饮食、音乐与名称让这种关系可读。

branches.en: TWO LABELS, ONE PERSON: passport and people are separated by the adjective.
branches.cn: 两个标签，一个人：形容词把护照与人群分开。

branches.en: THE OLD FAITH LINE: outside the covenant, the word once meant Gentile.
branches.cn: 旧的信仰界线：在盟约之外，这个词曾指外邦人。

branches.en: THE NOUN AND THE WAR: naming people as a category, and naming a war as ethnic, are both interpretations.
branches.cn: 名词与战争：把人命名为类别，把战争命名为族群冲突，都是一种解释。

intro.en: Ethnic is a Greek adjective transmitted through Latin; its stem ethno- is highly productive in the learned vocabulary.
intro.cn: ethnic 是经拉丁语传来的希腊形容词；其词干 ethno- 在学术词汇中构词能力很强。

latinIntro.en: Greek ethnos and ethnikos reach English through Latin ethnicus. The combining form ethno- is taken directly from Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 ethnos 与 ethnikos 经拉丁 ethnicus 抵达英语。构词成分 ethno- 直接取自希腊语。

items.example: Ethnicity is self-reported in the survey.
items.exampleCN: 调查中的族群身份由本人申报。

items.example: The town is ethnically diverse.
items.exampleCN: 这座镇子在族群上是多样的。

items.example: Ethnology grew out of museum collections.
items.exampleCN: 民族学从博物馆藏品中生长出来。

items.meaningCN: 民族志；基于田野的族群描述
items.example: The ethnography records daily speech.
items.exampleCN: 这份民族志记录了日常言谈。

items.example: An ethnocentric reading misses the loanwords.
items.exampleCN: 族群中心主义的读法会漏掉借词。

items.meaning: the habit of judging by one's own group
items.example: Ethnocentrism shaped the early accounts.
items.exampleCN: 族群中心主义塑造了早期记述。

items.meaning: the study of language and ethnicity together
items.example: Ethnolinguistics maps speech communities.
items.exampleCN: 族群语言学绘制言语共同体的地图。

items.example: The city is officially multi-ethnic.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市官方上是多族群的。

definition_zh: 族群；由共同祖先、语言或文化认同构成的人群；国家内部被承认的族裔群体
definition_en: a community of people who share ancestry, language or culture and are recognised as a distinct group
core_image: 一张村落分布图上，几个不同颜色的区块沿河谷排开，每个区块有自己的语言与节日
scene: 这个山谷里最大的一群人说着一种别处听不到的语言，节日也与他处不同。The valley's largest ethnic group speaks a language found nowhere else.
sceneCN: 这里 ethnic group 指由共同祖先、语言或文化构成的人群（第 1 个义项：作为共同体）；句意为这个山谷里最大的族群说着一种别处没有的语言。

pos.zh: 族群；族裔群体（可数）

collocations.phrase: an ethnic group within the state

derivatives.zh: 族群的（由希腊 ethnos 经拉丁进入，限定 group 的属性）
族群身份（由基础形容词加表抽象属性的名词后缀而来，由属性转指抽象身份）
群；组（经法语来自意大利语，指聚在一起的一簇人或物）
分组；归类（由基础动词加表活动或结果的名词后缀而来，由动作转指结果）
重新集结（由基础动词加表再次的前缀而来，由「聚成一组」转指「再次聚拢」）

senses.title: A community of shared origin
senses.definition: a people who trace common ancestry and share language, custom or memory
senses.definitionCN: 追溯共同祖先、共享语言、习俗或记忆的一群人
senses.example: Each ethnic group in the valley keeps its own harvest song.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷里的每个族群都保留自己的收割歌。
senses.why: The phrase joins a people to a body: group supplies the boundary, ethnic supplies what the boundary is drawn around.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组把人群与团体结合起来：团体提供边界，族群属性提供边界所圈定的内容。

senses.title: A recognised minority
senses.definition: a group officially or socially recognised as distinct within a larger state
senses.definitionCN: 在一个较大国家内被官方或社会承认为有区别的群体
senses.example: The constitution names five ethnic groups with protected rights.
senses.exampleCN: 宪法列出五个受权利保护的族群。
senses.why: Recognition is a legal act: a people becomes an ethnic group in law when the state names it.
senses.whyCN: 承认是一种法律行为：当国家点名时，一群人才在法律上成为族群。

senses.title: The analytic unit
senses.definition: the unit anthropologists and sociologists use to compare kinship, language and ritual
senses.definitionCN: 人类学者与社会学者用来比较亲属、语言与仪式的单位
senses.example: The study compared three ethnic groups across one generation.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究在一代人之内比较了三个族群。
senses.why: Research needs countable units; the phrase turns a fluid people into something that can be placed side by side.
senses.whyCN: 研究需要可数的单位；这个词组把流动的人群变成可以并排比较的对象。

senses.title: Self-identified membership
senses.definition: a group constituted by people who say they belong to it
senses.definitionCN: 由自称属于其中的人所构成的群体
senses.example: The ethnic group was defined by self-identification, not by a list.
senses.exampleCN: 这个族群靠自我认同来界定，而不是靠一份名单。
senses.why: Modern practice prefers the insider's claim; the group exists where members say it does.
senses.whyCN: 现代实践更看重内部人的主张；成员说它在，它就在。

senses.title: The majority group
senses.definition: the dominant ethnic group whose language and customs set the national norm
senses.definitionCN: 其语言与习俗设定国家规范的占主导地位的族群
senses.example: The majority ethnic group rarely notices its own ethnicity.
senses.exampleCN: 多数族群很少注意到自己的族群性。
senses.why: The phrase is not reserved for minorities: a majority is also an ethnic group, only one whose marks are invisible to itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组并非只用于少数群体：多数也是一个族群，只是它的标记对自己不可见。

senses.title: A political actor
senses.definition: a group organised to make claims on the state in the name of its people
senses.definitionCN: 以本族群之名向国家提出主张的组织化群体
senses.example: The ethnic group formed a party after the census.
senses.exampleCN: 普查之后，这个族群组成了一个政党。
senses.why: When a group acquires representatives, a cultural category becomes a bargaining unit.
senses.whyCN: 当一个群体有了代表，文化类别就变成了谈判单位。

senses.title: A census category
senses.definition: a box on official forms that counts people by ethnic membership
senses.definitionCN: 官方表格上按族群归属清点人口的选项
senses.example: The census lists the ethnic group under a new label.
senses.exampleCN: 普查用一种新标签列出这个族群。
senses.why: Counting requires a name and a fixed list, so the state's version of the group may differ from the group's own.
senses.whyCN: 清点需要一个名称和固定清单，因此国家版本的族群可能与族群自身的版本不同。

senses.title: Across borders
senses.definition: a people whose members live in several states and keep ties across borders
senses.definitionCN: 成员分布在若干国家、并维持跨境联系的群体
senses.example: The ethnic group operates schools in four countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个族群在四个国家办学校。
senses.why: Migration splits a group geographically without splitting its identity, so the phrase can cross state lines.
senses.whyCN: 迁徙把群体在地理上分开，却没有分开其认同，因此这个词组可以跨越国界。

intro.en: Ethnic group joins Greek ethnos 'people' (through ethnikos and Latin ethnicus) to group, a word borrowed from French and probably from Italian. The compound is a modern social-science term. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ethnic group 把希腊 ethnos「人群」（经 ethnikos 与拉丁 ethnicus）与 group 组合起来；后者借自法语，可能源自意大利语。这个复合词是现代社会科学术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Italian gruppo meant 'a cluster, a knot of things'. It is often derived from grappo 'knot', but the origin is uncertain and a Germanic source has also been proposed.
items.cn: 意大利语 gruppo 意为「一簇、一团」。它常被追溯到 grappo「结」，但来源不确定，也有人提出日耳曼语来源。

items.en: French groupe entered the language in the seventeenth century from Italian and named a cluster of figures in painting before it named people.
items.cn: 法语 groupe 在十七世纪从意大利语进入，先指绘画中聚在一起的人物群像，后指人群。

items.en: English group followed in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, widening from art to any set of things or persons gathered together.
items.cn: 英语 group 在十七、十八世纪跟进，从艺术用语扩展到任何聚在一起的事物或人。

items.en: Ethnos 'people, nation' supplied the first element; ethnikos and Latin ethnicus carried it into European languages.
items.cn: ethnos「人群、民族」提供前一成分；ethnikos 与拉丁 ethnicus 把它带入欧洲各语言。

items.en: In the twentieth century ethnic group became the standard unit for comparing peoples without the older language of race.
items.cn: 二十世纪，ethnic group 成为比较各人群的标准单位，取代了较早的种族语言。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of gruppo is unresolved, and the pre-Greek origin of ethnos remains unknown.
items.cn: 来源不确定：gruppo 的来源未有定论；ethnos 在希腊语之前的来源仍然不明。

note.en: Group one separates the parts of the phrase; group two holds other units for describing peoples.
note.cn: 第一组区分词组的组成部分；第二组是描述人群的其他单位。

entries.definition: The abstract belonging; the group is the people who hold it.
entries.definitionCN: 抽象的归属属性；族群则是持有这一属性的人们。

entries.definition: Describing a people; it needs a noun such as group to name the people itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述人群的；需要像 group 这样的名词才能命名人群本身。

entries.definition: Any set of persons or things; without ethnic it could be a chess club.
entries.definitionCN: 任何一组人或物；没有 ethnic 时也可能指棋社。

entries.definition: The arrangement of things into groups; it names a classification, not a people.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物分组的安排；它命名分类行为，而非一群人。

entries.definition: A group sharing a place or interest; it need not have common ancestry.
entries.definitionCN: 共享地点或利益的一群人；不一定有共同祖先。

entries.definition: A people claiming statehood or a whole state; larger and more political than an ethnic group.
entries.definitionCN: 主张国家地位的人群，或整个国家；比族群更大、更具政治性。

entries.definition: Any group smaller than the majority; ethnicity is one basis for minority status, not the only one.
entries.definitionCN: 任何小于多数群体的群体；族群性是少数地位的依据之一，而非唯一依据。

entries.definition: A kinship unit within a larger people; narrower than an ethnic group and based on descent lines.
entries.definitionCN: 较大人群内部的亲属单位；比族群窄，且以世系为基础。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real roots, real compounds and real social-science phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的词根、真实的复合词与真实的社会科学说法。

normal.en: Ethnic names the people, group names the boundary around them.
normal.cn: ethnic 命名人群，group 命名圈住他们的边界。

normal.en: Group first meant a cluster in a painting, then any cluster of people.
normal.cn: group 先指绘画中的一群人物，再指任何聚在一起的人。

normal.en: A majority is also an ethnic group; it simply does not notice its own marks.
normal.cn: 多数群体也是一个族群，只是它不注意自己的标记。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the analysis: ethnic group boundaries, relations between ethnic groups, the largest ethnic group.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出分析：族群边界、族群之间的关系、最大的族群。

normal.en: The plural ethnic groups is standard for comparisons and census lists.
normal.cn: 比较与普查清单中，复数 ethnic groups 是标准用法。

abstract.en: Picture a map coloured in blocks, where each colour also has a song.
abstract.cn: 想象一张用色块涂成的地图，每种颜色还各有一首歌。

abstract.en: Picture a circle drawn around a people, and the people moving across the line.
abstract.cn: 想象在人群周围画一个圈，而人不断越过那条线。

abstract.en: Picture a form with a box that fits one family badly and another family too well.
abstract.cn: 想象表格上的一个框，对一户人家太窄，对另一户又太宽。

examples.en: The ethnic group has kept its own calendar for centuries.
examples.cn: 这个族群数百年来保留着自己的历法。

examples.en: Census categories often split one ethnic group into two.
examples.cn: 普查类别常把一个族群拆成两个。

examples.en: Schools teach the history of every ethnic group in the province.
examples.cn: 学校教授本省每一个族群的历史。

dict_mnemonic.text: ethnic（族群的）+ group（聚成一群）＝ 因共同来源而聚成的一群人；记「一种语言，一圈边界，一张表格」。

root: ethnic 源自希腊 ethnos「人群」，更早来源不确定，经 ethnikos 与拉丁 ethnicus 传入英语；group 经法语来自意大利语 gruppo「一簇」，其来源不确定，或与「结」有关，或另有日耳曼语来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a shared-origin community to legal minority, analytic unit, self-identification, majority, political actor, census box and cross-border people.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从共享来源的共同体，移到法律上的少数、分析单位、自我认同、多数群体、政治行动者、普查选项与跨境人群。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coloured block on a map that also has a language, a festival and a line around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上一个色块，同时拥有一种语言、一个节日和一条围绕它的线。

branches.en: THE COMMUNITY: ancestry, language and memory held in common.
branches.cn: 共同体：共同持有的祖先、语言与记忆。

branches.en: THE LEGAL NAME: the state recognises the group and thereby fixes it.
branches.cn: 法律名称：国家承认这个群体，并因此把它固定下来。

branches.en: UNIT AND SELF-CLAIM: research counts it, while members say they belong.
branches.cn: 单位与自我主张：研究把它计数，成员则说自己属于其中。

branches.en: THE INVISIBLE MAJORITY: dominance hides its own ethnicity.
branches.cn: 看不见的多数：主导地位掩盖了自身的族群性。

branches.en: CLAIM, BOX AND BORDER: a party, a census category, and a people spread over several states.
branches.cn: 主张、表格与国界：一个政党、一个普查类别，以及分布于数个国家的人群。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek-derived adjective to a French-derived noun; both halves are common words in modern English.
intro.cn: 这个词组把希腊来源的形容词与法语来源的名词结合起来，两半都是现代英语常用词。

latinIntro.en: Only the first element is Greek-Latin: ethnos through ethnikos and ethnicus. Group is French and Italian, with an uncertain deeper origin.
latinIntro.cn: 只有前一成分属希腊—拉丁来源：ethnos 经 ethnikos 与 ethnicus。group 属法语与意大利语来源，更深来源不确定。

items.example: Ethnic lines are drawn by history.
items.exampleCN: 族群界线由历史画出。

items.example: The form asks about ethnicity.
items.exampleCN: 表格询问族群身份。

items.meaning: a cluster of people or things
items.example: The group meets on Sundays.
items.exampleCN: 这个群体周日见面。

items.example: The grouping follows language, not border.
items.exampleCN: 这种分组依据语言，而非国界。

items.example: The pupils sat in grouped desks.
items.exampleCN: 学生们坐在分组排列的课桌旁。

items.example: The marchers regrouped at the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 游行者在桥边重新集结。

items.meaning: the behaviour of people in a group
items.example: Group dynamics changed when the room filled.
items.exampleCN: 房间坐满后，群体动力发生了变化。

items.meaning: a smaller group inside a larger one
items.meaningCN: 子群；较大群体内的小群体
items.example: Each subgroup kept a separate dialect.
items.exampleCN: 每个子群保留了一种不同的方言。

definition_zh: 原住民族；世代生活在某地、先于外来定居者的族群；国际法意义上拥有独特制度与土地联系的人群
definition_en: peoples who have lived in a territory since before later settlers arrived and who keep distinct institutions and ties to the land
core_image: 海岸边的岩画上刻着潮水的刻度，讲解的人说这些刻度比任何航海图都早
scene: 海岸的岩壁上刻着潮水涨落的刻度，带队的人说这些刻度比任何航海图都早。The indigenous people of the coast have mapped the tides for centuries.
sceneCN: 这里 indigenous people 指世代生活在某地、先于外来定居者的族群（第 1 个义项：先于定居者的人群）；句意为海岸的原住民族已经为潮水作图数百年。

pos.zh: 原住民族；土著居民（复数，指某一地区的原住人群）
（国际法）原住民族（作为一个拥有集体权利的类别）

forms.label: 单数（指一个民族或一个人）

derivatives.zh: 原产的；土著的（由拉丁 indigena「本地出生」进入，核心是「生于其地」，是本词组的基础形容词）
原住民个体（由基础形容词的词干加表人的词尾而来，由性质转指人）
原住民性（由基础名词加表抽象属性的名词后缀而来，由人转指抽象属性）
人群；民族（经古法语来自拉丁 populus「人民」，由「一群人」转指「一个民族」）
诸民族（由「人群」一词的复数形式而来，用于区分多个有名称的人群）

senses.title: Peoples before settlers
senses.definition: communities living in a territory before later arrivals settled there
senses.definitionCN: 在后来者定居之前就生活在某片土地上的共同体
senses.example: The indigenous people of the valley were there long before the road.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷里的原住民族早在公路出现之前就在那里。
senses.why: Indigenous means born in the place; the phrase names priority in time, not a stage of development.
senses.whyCN: 前一个词意为生于其地；这个词组命名时间上的在先，而非发展阶段。

senses.title: A category in international law
senses.definition: peoples recognised as holding collective rights to land, culture and self-government
senses.definitionCN: 被承认对土地、文化与自治拥有集体权利的人群
senses.example: The declaration on the rights of indigenous people was adopted in 2007.
senses.exampleCN: 《原住民族权利宣言》于二零零七年获得通过。
senses.why: Law needs a defined subject; this sense turns a historical description into a holder of rights.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一个被界定的主体；这个义项把历史描述变成权利持有人。

senses.title: Distinct institutions
senses.definition: a people keeping its own language, law, medicine and forms of decision
senses.definitionCN: 保有自身语言、法律、医药与决策方式的人群
senses.example: The indigenous people settled disputes through their own councils.
senses.exampleCN: 这个原住民族通过自己的议事会解决纠纷。
senses.why: The category rests on difference that is institutional, not merely decorative: language and law must be maintained.
senses.whyCN: 这一类别建立在制度性的差异之上，而非装饰性差异：语言与法律必须被维持。

senses.title: First peoples of a region
senses.definition: the earliest known inhabitants of a particular land, often named by their own word for themselves
senses.definitionCN: 某一土地上已知最早的居民，常以其自称来命名
senses.example: The museum now names the indigenous people in their own language.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆现在用他们自己的语言称呼这支原住民族。
senses.why: Being first is local; the phrase can name one specific people in one specific landscape.
senses.whyCN: 「在先」是地方性的；这个词组可以命名某一片具体土地上的某一具体人群。

senses.title: Ties to land
senses.definition: a relationship to territory expressed through practice, story and seasonal use rather than a deed
senses.definitionCN: 通过实践、故事与季节性生活表达的土地关系，而非靠一纸地契
senses.example: For the indigenous people, the river is a relative, not a resource.
senses.exampleCN: 对这个原住民族来说，河流是亲属，不是资源。
senses.why: Land is not only property; this sense names a relation that law often struggles to translate.
senses.whyCN: 土地不只是财产；这个义项命名一种法律常难以转译的关系。

senses.title: Survivors of colonisation
senses.definition: peoples whose institutions and populations survived invasion, mission and resettlement
senses.definitionCN: 其制度与人口在入侵、传教与重新安置之后仍然存活的人群
senses.example: The indigenous people lost most of the island but kept the language.
senses.exampleCN: 这个原住民族失去了大部分岛屿，却保住了语言。
senses.why: The modern category is formed by loss; colonisation is the shared historical experience that gave it meaning.
senses.whyCN: 现代类别由失去所塑造；殖民是赋予它意义的共同历史经验。

senses.title: A collective in statistics and activism
senses.definition: an aggregate used by agencies and movements to speak of many distinct peoples at once
senses.definitionCN: 机构与运动用来同时指称许多不同民族的集合
senses.example: The census counted indigenous people in eight hundred villages.
senses.exampleCN: 普查清点了八百个村庄里的原住民族。
senses.why: Politics needs a large number; the phrase gathers very different peoples under one heading for counting and campaigning.
senses.whyCN: 政治需要一个大的数字；这个词组把非常不同的民族收进一个名目下，以便清点与动员。

senses.title: Self-naming versus outside label
senses.definition: the tension between a people's own name and the generic label applied from outside
senses.definitionCN: 一个民族自己的名称与外部施加的概括标签之间的张力
senses.example: The indigenous people prefer their own name to the official term.
senses.exampleCN: 这个原住民族更喜欢自己的名称，而非官方术语。
senses.why: Naming is power; the phrase can be correct in law and still be rejected by the people it describes.
senses.whyCN: 命名就是权力；这个词组在法律上可以正确，却仍可能被它所描述的人拒绝。

intro.en: Indigenous comes from Latin indigena 'native, born in the land', from indu 'in' plus gignere 'to beget'. People comes through Old French from Latin populus 'people', a word of uncertain origin. The English phrase is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: indigenous 来自拉丁 indigena「本地的、生于此地的」，由 indu「在内」加 gignere「生育」构成。people 经古法语来自拉丁 populus「人民」，其来源不确定。这个英语词组是现代的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Indigena meant 'a native, one born in a place', formed with indu, an old form of in, and the root gen- 'be born'. The adjective indigenus is parallel.
items.cn: indigena 意为「本地人、生于此地者」，由 indu（in 的旧形式）与表示「出生」的词根 gen- 构成。形容词 indigenus 与之并行。

items.en: Gignere 'to beget, bring forth' belongs to the gen- family that also gives genus, generate and native.
items.cn: gignere「生育、产生」属于 gen- 词族，该词族还给出 genus、generate 与 native。

items.en: Populus 'people' is the source of English people through Old French. Its own origin is uncertain; a link with Etruscan has been suggested but not proved.
items.cn: populus「人民」经古法语成为英语 people 的来源。它自身的来源不确定；有人提出与伊特鲁里亚语有关，但未获证明。

items.en: English indigenous appears in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries meaning 'native to a place', first of plants and animals as well as people.
items.cn: 英语 indigenous 在十六、十七世纪出现，意为「原产于某地」，最初既用于人，也用于动植物。

items.en: Indigenous people became a standard term of law and advocacy in the late twentieth century, especially with the 2007 UN declaration.
items.cn: indigenous people 在二十世纪后期成为法律与倡议的标准术语，尤其是在二零零七年联合国宣言之后。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of populus is unresolved; the deeper history of the gen- root is reconstructed; and the plural form peoples is used in law to mark distinct nations rather than one mass.
items.cn: 来源不确定：populus 的来源未有定论；gen- 词根更早的历史属重构形式；法律文本用复数 peoples 来标记不同民族，而非一整团人。

note.en: Group one separates words that look or sound close; group two holds alternative labels for original inhabitants.
note.cn: 第一组区分形近或音近的词；第二组是「原住居民」的其他称呼。

entries.definition: Poor, needy. It looks almost identical but comes from a different Latin word meaning 'lacking'.
entries.definitionCN: 贫穷的、匮乏的。拼写几乎相同，却来自另一个意为「缺少」的拉丁词。

entries.definition: A deep blue dye. It shares the opening letters but has nothing to do with birth or land.
entries.definitionCN: 一种深蓝色染料。开头字母相同，却与出生或土地无关。

entries.definition: Native to a place; alone it can describe a plant, a language or a species, not only people.
entries.definitionCN: 原产于某地的；单用时可形容植物、语言或物种，不只指人。

entries.definition: Born in a place; it is broader and can describe anyone born locally, not only original peoples.
entries.definitionCN: 生于某地的；范围更宽，可以指任何本地出生的人，而不只是原住民族。

entries.definition: A term used especially in Canada and Australia; it stresses priority in time without the Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 尤其在加拿大与澳大利亚使用的说法；强调时间上的在先，而不带拉丁词根。

entries.definition: Original inhabitants of a land, from Latin ab origine 'from the beginning'; in some countries it is the official term.
entries.definitionCN: 某地的原住居民，来自拉丁「从起初」；在有些国家它是官方术语。

entries.definition: The locally born residents of an area; it can include settlers' descendants and is not a legal category.
entries.definitionCN: 某地本地出生的居民；可以包括定居者的后代，且不是法律类别。

entries.definition: Peoples organised in tribes; it describes a social form rather than a historical or legal status.
entries.definitionCN: 以部落组织的人群；它描述社会形式，而非历史或法律地位。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin parts, real legal terms and real alternative labels.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件、真实的法律术语与真实的替代称呼。

normal.en: Indigenous means born inside the land: the old preposition for 'in' plus the root for birth.
normal.cn: indigenous 意为生在这片土地之内：表示「在内」的旧介词加「出生」词根。

normal.en: The same birth root gives native and nation, so indigenous, native and nation are cousins.
normal.cn: 同一个「出生」词根给出 native 与 nation，所以 indigenous、native、nation 是表亲。

normal.en: Keep indigent apart: it means needy, not native.
normal.cn: 把 indigent 分开：它意为贫穷，而不是原产。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the legal field: indigenous people's rights, indigenous people and local communities.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出法律领域：原住民族权利、原住民族与当地社区。

normal.en: In law, peoples is plural to mark distinct nations rather than one undifferentiated mass.
normal.cn: 在法律文本中，peoples 用复数来标记不同民族，而非一整团没有区分的人。

abstract.en: Picture a rock covered in tide marks older than any chart.
abstract.cn: 想象一块岩石，上面刻着比任何航海图都古老的潮位记号。

abstract.en: Picture a deed that cannot describe a river, because the river is a relative.
abstract.cn: 想象一纸地契无法描述一条河，因为那条河是亲属。

abstract.en: Picture a name chosen by the people and a label chosen by the office.
abstract.cn: 想象一个由人群自己选定的名字，和一个由机关选定的标签。

examples.en: The indigenous people manage the forest with fire, not with fences.
examples.cn: 这个原住民族用火管理森林，而不是用围栏。

examples.en: Treaties with indigenous people were signed and then ignored.
examples.cn: 与原住民族签订的条约被签下，随后被无视。

examples.en: The school invites indigenous people to teach the local language.
examples.cn: 学校邀请原住民族来教授当地语言。

dict_mnemonic.text: indigena（生在此地）+ people（人群）＝ 生在这片土地上的人；记「先来的人，后来的路」。

root: indigenous 源自拉丁 indigena「本地出生者」，由 indu「在内」加 gignere「生育」构成，词根 gen- 的更早形式属重构；people 经古法语来自拉丁 populus「人民」，populus 的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from priority in time to legal category, distinct institutions, local first peoples, land ties, colonial survival, statistical aggregation and the politics of naming.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从时间上的在先，移到法律类别、独特制度、地方先住民、土地联系、殖民后的存续、统计集合与命名政治。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: tide marks cut into rock long before the first chart was drawn.
core.cn: 核心意象：在最早的航海图出现之前，潮位记号就已刻进岩石。

branches.en: PRIORITY IN PLACE: a people already there, and one specific people in one landscape.
branches.cn: 地方上的在先：一群早已在那里的人，以及某片土地上的某一具体人群。

branches.en: LOSS BECOMES LAW: colonial survival produces the legal subject that claims rights.
branches.cn: 失去变成法律：殖民后的存续产生出主张权利的法律主体。

branches.en: KEPT INSTITUTIONS: language, law and councils carry the difference.
branches.cn: 被保住的制度：语言、法律与议事会承载着差异。

branches.en: THE RIVER AS RELATIVE: land is a relation, not only a deed.
branches.cn: 河流即亲属：土地是一种关系，不只是地契。

branches.en: COUNTED AND NAMED: agencies gather many peoples into one figure, while the peoples choose their own names.
branches.cn: 被计数与被命名：机构把许多民族汇成一个数字，而各民族选择自己的名称。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin adjective of local birth to a Latin noun for a people; both halves are learned borrowings.
intro.cn: 这个词组把表示「本地出生」的拉丁形容词与表示「人民」的拉丁名词结合起来，两半都是学术借词。

latinIntro.en: Indigena and gignere supply the first element; populus, through Old French, supplies the second. Populus has no proven Latin derivation.
latinIntro.cn: indigena 与 gignere 提供前一成分；populus 经古法语提供后一成分。populus 没有已证实的拉丁派生来源。

items.example: The palm is indigenous to the island.
items.exampleCN: 这种棕榈原产于该岛。

items.example: The law uses indigene in its French text.
items.exampleCN: 该法律的法语文本使用 indigene 一词。

items.example: Indigeneity is recognised by institutions as well as by descent.
items.exampleCN: 原住民性既由制度承认，也由世系确认。

items.example: She is a native speaker of the language.
items.exampleCN: 她是这门语言的母语者。

items.example: The nation includes many peoples.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家包含许多民族。

items.structure: populus (Latin n.) via Old French people
items.meaning: a body of persons; a nation
items.example: The people of the coast keep the old calendar.
items.exampleCN: 海岸的人们保留着旧历法。

items.meaningCN: 诸民族；多个有名称的人群
items.example: The charter speaks of peoples, not populations.
items.exampleCN: 该宪章说的是诸民族，而不是人口。

items.meaning: the people counted in a place
items.meaningCN: 人口；某地被清点的人群
items.example: The population includes both groups.
items.exampleCN: 人口中包括这两个群体。

items.example: The song became popular far from home.
items.exampleCN: 这首歌在远方变得流行。

latinEntries.structure: indu (Latin preposition, old form of in)

definition_zh: 出生的；本地的；原产的；天生的；（计算机）原生的；本地居民；原住民
definition_en: born in or belonging naturally to a particular place, and hence original or inborn
core_image: 一株只长在这面山坡的野花，根须抓住本地的碎石，移栽到别处便枯死
scene: 这面山坡上只长这一种野花，移栽到别处总活不成。The plant is native to this slope and nowhere else.
sceneCN: 这里 native 指原产于某地的（第 2 个义项：天然属于某地）；句意为这种植物原产于这面山坡，别处没有。

pos.zh: 出生的；本地的（指生于某地或天然属于某地）
天生的；固有的（指与生俱来的性质）
（计算机）原生的（为某平台原生开发）
本地人；原住民（可数）

derivatives.zh: 原生地；天生地（由基础形容词加表方式的副词后缀而来，由性质转指方式）
出生；诞生（由拉丁词干加表抽象属性的名词后缀而来，由「出生的」转指「出生」这一事件）
本地出生的（由基础形容词与表出生的成分复合而成，由「出生」转指「生于本地」的身份）
本族性；母语程度（由基础形容词加表抽象状态的名词后缀而来，由性质转指抽象状态）
民族；国家（由拉丁同一词干加表过程或结果的名词后缀而来，同一「出生」词根，由「出生的人群」转指「民族」）

senses.title: Born in a place
senses.definition: having been born in a particular place or country
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地方或国家出生的
senses.example: She is a native of the coastal town and knows every lane.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这座海滨小镇本地出生的人，认得每一条小巷。
senses.why: The Latin root is birth itself; the adjective begins as a plain statement about where someone was born.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根本身就是「出生」；这个形容词起初只是关于出生地的平实陈述。

senses.title: Belonging to a place naturally
senses.definition: growing or living naturally in a region and not introduced from elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 在某地区自然生长或生活，而非从别处引入的
senses.example: The plant is native to this slope and nowhere else.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物原产于这面山坡，别处没有。
senses.why: The same birth relation applies to species: a plant is 'born' in its range and does not need a person to place it there.
senses.whyCN: 同样的出生关系也适用于物种：植物在其分布区内「出生」，不需要人把它放到那里。

senses.title: Indigenous person
senses.definition: a member of the peoples who lived in a territory before later settlers
senses.definitionCN: 在后来定居者之前就生活于某片土地的民族的成员
senses.example: The treaty was signed with the native inhabitants, not with the settlers.
senses.exampleCN: 条约是与原住居民签订的，而不是与定居者。
senses.why: The noun turns the birth relation into a political identity, and modern usage often prefers indigenous for this sense.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式把出生关系变成政治身份；现代用法在这一义项上更常用「原住民族」这一说法。

senses.title: Inborn quality
senses.definition: present from birth rather than learned or acquired
senses.definitionCN: 出生时就有、而非习得或获得的
senses.example: He has a native talent for hearing pitch.
senses.exampleCN: 他有分辨音高的天赋。
senses.why: If native means born with a place, it can also mean born with a quality; the metaphor moves from location to nature.
senses.whyCN: 如果这个词指「生在某地」，它也能指「生来带有某种性质」；这个比喻从地点移到了天性。

senses.title: Unmixed material
senses.definition: found in a pure form in nature, as of metals
senses.definitionCN: 在自然界以纯净形态存在，如某些金属
senses.example: The riverbed holds native copper, not ore.
senses.exampleCN: 河床里有天然铜，而不是矿石。
senses.why: A metal 'native to the earth' is one that nature left uncombined; the sense narrows to chemical purity.
senses.whyCN: 「生在大地之中」的金属，就是自然留下、未经化合的那种；词义收窄到化学纯度。

senses.title: Built for a platform
senses.definition: designed to run directly on a particular operating system or device
senses.definitionCN: 为某一操作系统或设备直接运行而设计的
senses.example: The native app opens faster than the web version.
senses.exampleCN: 原生应用比网页版打开得更快。
senses.why: Computing borrows the word for belonging: software native to a system needs no translator layer.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借用了「属于」这一含义：属于某系统的软件不需要转译层。

senses.title: First-learned language
senses.definition: the language a person acquired in childhood, often called the mother tongue
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在童年习得的语言，常称为母语
senses.example: Her native language is not the one she writes in now.
senses.exampleCN: 她的母语并不是她现在写作所用的语言。
senses.why: Language is acquired at birth-time, so the adjective marks the earliest layer of speech rather than national origin.
senses.whyCN: 语言在出生时期被习得，因此这个形容词标记言语的最早层次，而非国籍。

senses.title: A local resident
senses.definition: a person who lives in a place by birth rather than by recent arrival
senses.definitionCN: 因出生而居住在某地、而非近期到来的人
senses.example: The shopkeeper is a native but the cook arrived last year.
senses.exampleCN: 店主是本地人，厨师则是去年才来的。
senses.why: In everyday use the noun simply contrasts old residents with newcomers, with no legal weight.
senses.whyCN: 在日常用法中，这个名词只是把老居民与新来者对照，没有法律分量。

senses.title: The colonial label
senses.definition: the dated and often demeaning use of the noun for colonised peoples
senses.definitionCN: 殖民时代用来指被殖民人群的过时且常含贬抑的名词用法
senses.example: Colonial reports used the noun in a way that modern editors avoid.
senses.exampleCN: 殖民报告使用这个名词的方式，现代编辑会回避。
senses.why: A neutral birth word can be turned into a category of rule; this sense names that history rather than endorsing it.
senses.whyCN: 一个中性的出生词可以被变成统治的类别；这个义项命名那段历史，而非认可它。

intro.en: Native comes from Latin nativus 'innate, born', from nasci 'to be born', whose older form gnasci belongs to the gen- root seen in genus and generate. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: native 来自拉丁 nativus「天生的、出生的」，源自动词 nasci「出生」，其更早形式 gnasci 属于 gen- 词根，该词根也见于 genus 与 generate。年代均为约数。

items.en: Nasci 'to be born, to arise' is a deponent verb; its older form gnasci shows the initial g that survives in cognate words.
items.cn: nasci「出生、产生」是异态动词；其更早形式 gnasci 显示出词首的 g，这个 g 在同族词中保留下来。

items.en: Nativus meant 'innate, natural, born with one', and also 'of birth'. It could describe a person born in a place and a quality present from birth.
items.cn: nativus 意为「天生的、自然的、生来带有的」，也指「出生的」。它既能描述生于某地的人，也能描述与生俱来的性质。

items.en: The gen- root 'to be born, beget' is reconstructed; it also underlies genus, genius, generate and nation. The reconstruction is standard but the exact ablaut grades are reconstructed forms.
items.cn: 表示「出生、生育」的 gen- 词根属重构；它也是 genus、genius、generate 与 nation 的基础。这一重构是通行的，但具体的元音交替形式均属重构。

items.en: Old French natif carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of inborn and later of local birth.
items.cn: 古法语 natif 在十四世纪把该词带入英语，先表示「天生的」，后表示「本地出生的」。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the noun was used by settlers for the peoples they colonised, a usage now recognised as demeaning and largely replaced.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，这个名词被定居者用来指他们所殖民的人群；这一用法如今被认定为贬抑性的，且多被取代。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact pre-Latin shape of the birth root is a reconstruction, and the date at which the computing sense appeared is not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个「出生」词根在拉丁语之前的确切形状属重构形式；计算机义项出现的年代也没有精确固定。

note.en: Group one separates near neighbours from the same birth root; group two holds words for original belonging.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一「出生」词根的近邻词；第二组表示原初归属。

entries.definition: A people or state, from the same birth root; it names a collectivity, while native names a relation.
entries.definitionCN: 民族或国家，同出「出生」词根；它命名一个集合，而 native 命名一种关系。

entries.definition: Relating to birth, as in natal care; it is medical and temporal, with no sense of belonging to a place.
entries.definitionCN: 与出生有关的，如产后护理；它属医学与时间用法，不含「属于某地」之意。

entries.definition: A birth, especially the Nativity; it names the event rather than a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 出生，尤指耶稣诞生；它命名事件，而非性质。

entries.definition: Lacking experience; it comes from French naive, from Latin nativus 'natural', but developed the sense of unworldly.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏经验的；来自法语 naive，再上溯拉丁 nativus「自然的」，但发展出「不通世故」之义。

entries.definition: Native to a territory before settlers; it is the preferred term in law and advocacy.
entries.definitionCN: 先于定居者而原产于某地；它是法律与倡议中更受青睐的说法。

entries.definition: Of a nearby place; it says nothing about birth or priority.
entries.definitionCN: 属于附近地方的；不涉及出生或时间在先。

entries.definition: Present from birth as a quality; it covers only the innate sense of native.
entries.definitionCN: 作为性质与生俱来的；只覆盖 native 的天生义。

entries.definition: Found only in one region, often of species or disease; it stresses restriction rather than birth.
entries.definitionCN: 仅见于某一地区，常用于物种或疾病；强调局限，而非出生。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real birth root, its real relatives and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「出生」词根、其真实同族词与真实的固定说法。

normal.en: Native means born: the same root gives nation, natal and nativity.
normal.cn: native 意为「出生的」：同一词根给出 nation、natal、nativity。

normal.en: A plant native to a slope is 'born' there; a native speaker was 'born into' the language.
normal.cn: 原产山坡的植物是在那里「出生」的；母语者是被「生进」那门语言的。

normal.en: Native copper is metal nature left unmixed, the chemical version of 'belonging to the earth'.
normal.cn: 天然铜是自然留下、未经混合的金属，即「属于大地」的化学版本。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: native speaker, native species, native to, a native of.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出范围：母语者、本地物种、原产于、本地出生的人。

normal.en: The plural natives is neutral only for local residents; for peoples, indigenous is safer.
normal.cn: 复数 natives 只在指本地居民时中性；指民族时，用 indigenous 更稳妥。

abstract.en: Picture a root system that refuses to hold in foreign gravel.
abstract.cn: 想象一套根须，在陌生的碎石里怎么也抓不住。

abstract.en: Picture a word learned at a kitchen table before any classroom.
abstract.cn: 想象一个在饭桌旁、任何教室之前就学会的词。

abstract.en: Picture software that speaks the machine's own language without an interpreter.
abstract.cn: 想象一种软件，不用翻译就说着机器自己的语言。

examples.en: The eucalyptus is native to Australia but grows all over the world now.
examples.cn: 桉树原产于澳大利亚，如今却长遍世界。

examples.en: A native speaker may still not know why a sentence is grammatical.
examples.cn: 母语者仍可能不知道一个句子为何合乎语法。

examples.en: The app was rebuilt as a native version for each platform.
examples.cn: 这个应用被重做成各平台的原生版本。

dict_mnemonic.text: nasci（出生）+ ive（……的）＝ 生来就在这里的；记「根不肯离开这面坡」。

root: 源自拉丁 nativus「天生的、出生的」，来自动词 nasci「出生」，其更早形式为 gnasci；其词根 gen- 属原始印欧语重构形式，也见于 genus、generate 与 nation。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow birth from a place to species, peoples, innate qualities, pure metals, software platforms, first languages, local residency and the colonial label.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿着「出生」展开：从出生地，到物种、民族、天生性质、纯净金属、软件平台、母语、本地居民，以及殖民时代的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a root that holds only in its own gravel.
core.cn: 核心意象：一套只在本乡碎石里才抓得住的根。

branches.en: BIRTH AT TWO SCALES: born in a place, and born into a language.
branches.cn: 两种尺度的出生：生于某地，以及生入一门语言。

branches.en: NATURE AND HISTORY: a species belongs to its range, and a people belongs before settlers.
branches.cn: 自然与历史：物种属于其分布区，民族则先于定居者而属于那里。

branches.en: INWARD AND PURE: a quality present at birth, and a metal left unmixed.
branches.cn: 向内与纯净：出生时就在的性质，以及未经混合的金属。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: software native to a system needs no translator.
branches.cn: 机器：属于某系统的软件不需要转译。

branches.en: RESIDENT AND LABEL: the neutral local, and the colonial noun that modern usage rejects.
branches.cn: 居民与标签：中性的本地人，以及现代用法拒斥的殖民名词。

intro.en: Native is a Latin adjective of birth; its stem also builds a family of English words about origins.
intro.cn: native 是表示「出生」的拉丁形容词；其词干还构成一批关于来源的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin nasci and nativus supply the base; the same gen- root reaches English in genus, generate, nation and natal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 nasci 与 nativus 提供基础；同一 gen- 词根经 genus、generate、nation 与 natal 进入英语。

items.example: The format is natively supported.
items.exampleCN: 这种格式被原生支持。

items.example: Tests cannot measure nativeness directly.
items.exampleCN: 测试无法直接测量母语程度。

items.example: The church celebrates the Nativity in December.
items.exampleCN: 教堂在十二月庆祝耶稣诞生。

items.example: Native-born citizens and immigrants share the district.
items.exampleCN: 本地出生公民与移民共居这个区。

items.example: The nation was built from many regions.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家由许多地区构建而成。

items.example: The question became a national debate.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题成了全国性的辩论。

items.example: Natal care reduced infant mortality.
items.exampleCN: 围产期护理降低了婴儿死亡率。

items.example: Some abilities are innate rather than taught.
items.exampleCN: 有些能力是天生的，而非教出来的。

definition_zh: 原住人口；某地原有的人群；本地出生居民的总数；（统计）原住民族人口
definition_en: the people original to a territory, or the locally born residents of a place, counted as a group
core_image: 一张人口曲线图上，一条线在某个年份陡然下落，旁边注着「原住人口」
scene: 档案里那张人口曲线在某一年陡然下落，旁边的注记只写了短短一行。The native population fell sharply after the first epidemic.
sceneCN: 这里 native population 指某地原有的人群总数（第 1 个义项：原有居民整体）；句意为第一次疫病之后，原住人口急剧下降。

pos.zh: 原住人口；本地出生居民（不可数集合名词，也可加不定冠词指一个群体）

collocations.phrase: the native population of the island
a decline in the native population

forms.label: 复数（指多个地区的原住人口）

derivatives.zh: 本地的；原产的（由拉丁 nativus「出生的」进入，限定 population 的来源）
人口；种群（由拉丁 populus「人民」加表过程的名词后缀而来，由「人民」转指「被清点的人群」）
居住于；使有人口（由「人口」一词的动词形式而来，由「人群」转指「使人住满」）
人口稠密的（由拉丁词干加表性质的形容词后缀而来，由「人民」转指「人多的」）
使人口减少（由基础动词加表相反或去除的前缀而来，由「住满」反向转为「使人走空」）

senses.title: The original inhabitants
senses.definition: the people living in a territory before later settlers arrived
senses.definitionCN: 在后来定居者到来之前就生活在某片土地上的人
senses.example: The native population of the island had names for every reef.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的原住人口给每一处暗礁都取了名字。
senses.why: Native marks priority in time; population supplies the counted body, so the phrase names those who were there first as a whole.
senses.whyCN: 前一个词标记时间上的在先，后一个词提供被清点的整体，因此这个词组命名先在那里的人的总和。

senses.title: A demographic category
senses.definition: the number of indigenous people recorded in a census or survey
senses.definitionCN: 普查或调查中记录的原住民族人数
senses.example: The native population was undercounted in the first census.
senses.exampleCN: 第一次普查中，原住人口被少算了。
senses.why: Counting needs a category; the phrase turns a people into a figure that can be compared across years.
senses.whyCN: 清点需要一个类别；这个词组把人群变成一个可以跨年比较的数字。

senses.title: Locally born residents
senses.definition: everyone born in a place, as opposed to immigrants and their children
senses.definitionCN: 在某地出生的所有人，相对于移民及其子女
senses.example: The native population and the newcomers use different schools.
senses.exampleCN: 本地出生居民与新来者上不同的学校。
senses.why: Here native is the mild everyday contrast with foreign-born, with no claim about who came first historically.
senses.whyCN: 这里的前一个词是与「外国出生」相对的温和日常对照，并不主张历史上谁先到。

senses.title: Population before colonisation
senses.definition: the size and composition of a people at the moment before outside rule began
senses.definitionCN: 外来统治开始之前那一刻，一个人群的数量与构成
senses.example: Historians estimate the native population before the missions arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学者估算传教团到来之前的原住人口。
senses.why: The phrase can mark a baseline: everything after it is measured as loss or change from that point.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组可以标记一条基线：此后的一切都被当作相对该点的损失或变化来度量。

senses.title: A people with legal standing
senses.definition: the indigenous peoples of a state considered as holders of collective rights
senses.definitionCN: 被视为集体权利持有者的某国原住民族
senses.example: The law recognises the native population as a distinct legal community.
senses.exampleCN: 法律承认原住人口为一个独特的法律共同体。
senses.why: Law addresses a body, not a list of individuals; population can name that collective subject.
senses.whyCN: 法律面对的是一个整体，而不是一份个人名单；后一个词可以命名那个集体主体。

senses.title: A group measured over time
senses.definition: the object of fertility, mortality and migration statistics
senses.definitionCN: 出生率、死亡率与迁徙统计所度量的对象
senses.example: The native population grew again only after the clinics opened.
senses.exampleCN: 直到诊所开设之后，原住人口才再次增长。
senses.why: Demography needs a denominator; this sense treats the people as a quantity whose changes can be tracked.
senses.whyCN: 人口学需要一个底数；这个义项把人群当作一个可以追踪变化的数量。

senses.title: The local workforce
senses.definition: the residents born in a place who supply its labour, as opposed to imported workers
senses.definitionCN: 在某地出生、为其提供劳动力的居民，相对于外来工人
senses.example: The mine hired the native population before bringing in outsiders.
senses.exampleCN: 矿场先雇用本地人口，之后才引进外来者。
senses.why: Economic policy also counts who is local; the phrase shifts from culture to labour supply.
senses.whyCN: 经济政策也要清点谁算本地人；这个词组从文化转向劳动力供给。

senses.title: A colonial administrative label
senses.definition: the category used by colonial offices to classify and count the colonised
senses.definitionCN: 殖民官署用来分类并清点被殖民者的类别
senses.example: Colonial records split the native population into invented tribes.
senses.exampleCN: 殖民档案把原住人口拆成若干被发明出来的部落。
senses.why: Administration often manufactured the categories it counted; this sense names that bureaucratic act.
senses.whyCN: 行政常常制造出它所清点的类别；这个义项命名那种官僚行为。

intro.en: Native comes from Latin nativus 'born', from nasci 'to be born'. Population comes from Late Latin populatio 'a peopling', from populus 'people', a word of uncertain origin. The English phrase is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: native 来自拉丁 nativus「出生的」，源自动词 nasci「出生」。population 来自晚期拉丁 populatio「使人居住」，词根 populus「人民」来源不确定。这个英语词组是现代的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Nasci 'to be born' has the older form gnasci and belongs to the gen- root for birth, also seen in genus and nation.
items.cn: nasci「出生」有更早形式 gnasci，属于表示「出生」的 gen- 词根，该词根也见于 genus 与 nation。

items.en: Populus 'people' is the base of populatio and population. Its own origin is uncertain; a link with Etruscan has been suggested but not proved.
items.cn: populus「人民」是 populatio 与 population 的基础。它自身的来源不确定；有人提出与伊特鲁里亚语有关，但未获证明。

items.en: Populatio could mean 'a laying waste' from populari 'to ravage', and also 'a peopling' from populare 'to people'. English population comes from the second, not the first.
items.cn: populatio 既可指「荒废、劫掠」（来自 populari「毁坏」），也可指「使人居住」（来自 populare「使人住」）。英语 population 来自后者，而非前者。

items.en: English population appears in the sixteenth century meaning 'a peopled land'; the statistical sense of a counted body of people develops later.
items.cn: 英语 population 在十六世纪出现，意为「有人居住的地方」；被清点的人口这一统计义后来才发展出来。

items.en: Native population became a standard phrase in colonial administration, demography and indigenous-rights discourse, each giving it a different accent.
items.cn: native population 在殖民行政、人口学与原住民族权利话语中都成了标准说法，各自给它不同的侧重。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of populus is unresolved, and the pre-Latin shape of the birth root is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定：populus 的来源未有定论；「出生」词根在拉丁语之前的形状属重构，而非有直接书证。

note.en: Group one separates the two halves of the phrase; group two holds terms for counted peoples.
note.cn: 第一组区分词组的两个部分；第二组是被清点人群的术语。

entries.definition: Peoples original to a territory; it is the standard term in law and advocacy, with clearer collective rights.
entries.definitionCN: 某地原有的民族；它是法律与倡议中的标准术语，集体权利含义更清楚。

entries.definition: Any counted group of people; without native it says nothing about origin.
entries.definitionCN: 任何被清点的人群；没有 native 时不涉及来源。

entries.definition: Born in a place; alone it can modify a speaker, a species or a app.
entries.definitionCN: 生于某地的；单用时可修饰母语者、物种或应用。

entries.definition: The birth rate of a population; it looks close to native but belongs to demography, not origin.
entries.definitionCN: 人口出生率；看起来与 native 相近，却属人口学，与来源无关。

entries.definition: The people of a particular area, whether born there or not; it makes no claim about priority.
entries.definitionCN: 某一地区的人，不论是否在那里出生；不主张时间在先。

entries.definition: Those who lived in a place first; it is descriptive and carries no legal status.
entries.definitionCN: 最早居住在某地的人；属描述性说法，不带法律地位。

entries.definition: The incoming colonists and their descendants; it is the phrase's usual opposite in colonial history.
entries.definitionCN: 到来的殖民者及其后代；在殖民史中常是这个词组的对立面。

entries.definition: The citizens of a state as a body; it is a legal category, not an origin category.
entries.definitionCN: 一个国家的公民整体；它是法律类别，而非来源类别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin parts, real demographic phrases and real historical usage.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件、真实的人口学说法与真实的历史用法。

normal.en: Native gives the origin, population gives the count.
normal.cn: native 给出来源，population 给出数量。

normal.en: Population comes from 'people', not from 'populate the land' in the sense of filling it up.
normal.cn: population 来自「人民」，而不是「把土地填满」那个意思。

normal.en: The same Latin noun could mean both peopling and laying waste; English took the peaceful one.
normal.cn: 同一个拉丁名词既能指「使人居住」，也能指「毁坏」；英语取的是和平的那个。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the uses: the native population of the island, a decline in the native population, native population density.
normal.cn: 固定说法显示用法：该岛的原住人口、原住人口的下降、本地人口密度。

normal.en: The plural native populations compares several territories, not several individuals.
normal.cn: 复数 native populations 比较的是多个地区，而不是多个个人。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a graph that drops at the exact year a ship arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象图线上的一条线，恰在一艘船抵达的那一年下落。

abstract.en: Picture a census that counts people it has already sorted into invented boxes.
abstract.cn: 想象一次普查，清点的是它自己先分进发明出来的框里的人。

abstract.en: Picture a school where two groups learn separately in the same building.
abstract.cn: 想象一所学校，两个群体在同一栋楼里分开上课。

examples.en: The native population had no word for the border until the map arrived.
examples.cn: 在地图到来之前，原住人口没有「边界」这个词。

examples.en: Vaccination reached the native population last and the toll was highest there.
examples.cn: 疫苗最后才到达原住人口，那里的死亡也最多。

examples.en: The native population of the valley is now a minority in its own land.
examples.cn: 山谷的原住人口如今在自己的土地上成了少数。

dict_mnemonic.text: native（生在此地）+ population（被清点的人群）＝ 生在此地、被一起数进去的人；记「一条线下落的那一年」。

root: native 源自拉丁 nativus「出生的」，来自动词 nasci，词根 gen- 属重构；population 源自晚期拉丁 populatio「使人居住」，其词根 populus「人民」来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from original inhabitants to census category, local-born residents, pre-colonial baseline, legal community, measured quantity, labour supply and colonial label.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从原有居民，移到普查类别、本地出生居民、殖民前基线、法律共同体、被度量的数量、劳动力供给与殖民标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a graph line that drops at the year a ship arrives.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条在船只抵达那一年下落的曲线。

branches.en: BEFORE AND AT THE START: those already there, and the baseline at the moment before outside rule.
branches.cn: 先在与此刻：早已在那里的人，以及外来统治开始前那一刻的基线。

branches.en: THE FIGURE: a category in the census, then a quantity tracked through births and deaths.
branches.cn: 数字：普查中的一个类别，再是通过出生与死亡被追踪的数量。

branches.en: THE LOCAL POOL: born residents contrasted with newcomers, and the same people as a labour supply.
branches.cn: 本地储备：本地出生者与新来者的对照，以及同一批人作为劳动力。

branches.en: THE LEGAL BODY: a collective that can hold rights.
branches.cn: 法律整体：一个可以持有权利的集体。

branches.en: THE INVENTED BOX: colonial offices manufactured the categories they counted.
branches.cn: 被发明的框：殖民官署制造出自己所清点的类别。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin adjective of birth to a Latin noun of counted people; both halves are learned borrowings.
intro.cn: 这个词组把表示「出生」的拉丁形容词与表示「被清点人群」的拉丁名词结合起来，两半都是学术借词。

latinIntro.en: Nativus and nasci supply the first element; populus and populatio supply the second. Populus has no proven derivation.
latinIntro.cn: nativus 与 nasci 提供前一成分；populus 与 populatio 提供后一成分。populus 没有已证实的派生来源。

items.example: The native residents kept the old wells.
items.exampleCN: 本地居民保留着旧水井。

items.meaning: the people counted in a place
items.example: The population doubled in ten years.
items.exampleCN: 人口在十年内翻了一番。

items.example: Settlers populated the lower valley.
items.exampleCN: 定居者使下游山谷有了人烟。

items.example: The coast is the most populous district.
items.exampleCN: 沿海是最人口稠密的地区。

items.meaning: to reduce the people of a place
items.example: War depopulated the uplands.
items.exampleCN: 战争使高地人口锐减。

items.example: The populace gathered in the square.
items.exampleCN: 民众聚集在广场上。

items.example: The reform was popular in the villages.
items.exampleCN: 这项改革在村里很受欢迎。

items.example: Natality fell below replacement.
items.exampleCN: 出生率降到了更替水平以下。

definition_zh: 社会凝聚力；把社会成员维系在一起的力量；共享价值、信任与归属的程度
definition_en: the strength of the bonds, shared norms and trust that hold the members of a society together
core_image: 一张网把许多彼此陌生的院子连起来，线不粗，但每一根都绷着
scene: 节日和共用学校把这个分裂的镇子慢慢连了起来，陌生人开始互相点头。Festivals and shared schools built social cohesion across the divided town.
sceneCN: 这里 social cohesion 指把社会成员维系在一起的力量（第 1 个义项：整体联结力）；句意为节日与共用学校在这个分裂的镇子上建立了社会凝聚力。

pos.zh: 社会凝聚力（不可数，指社会联结的程度）

derivatives.zh: 黏合；连贯（由拉丁 cohaerere「黏在一起」进入，核心是「彼此粘住」，是本词组的基础动词）
凝聚力（由基础动词加表过程或状态的名词后缀而来，由动作转指状态）
有凝聚力的（由「凝聚力」一词的形容词形式而来，由状态转指性质）
社会的（由拉丁 socialis「同伴的」进入，限定联结的范围）
连贯的（由拉丁词根加表共同的前缀，构成另一形容词形式，由「粘住」转指「说得通」）

senses.title: The glue of a society
senses.definition: the overall strength of the ties that keep a population together as one society
senses.definitionCN: 把一个全体人口维系为一个社会的各种纽带的总强度
senses.example: The survey measured social cohesion after the strike.
senses.exampleCN: 罢工之后，调查测量了社会凝聚力。
senses.why: Cohesion is sticking together; social limits the sticking to a whole society rather than a team or a text.
senses.whyCN: 后一个词是黏在一起；前一个词把这种黏合限定到整个社会，而不是团队或文本。

senses.title: Shared norms and trust
senses.definition: the common expectations and mutual confidence that let people cooperate with strangers
senses.definitionCN: 让陌生人可以合作的那些共同期待与相互信任
senses.example: Social cohesion depends on people trusting the same rules.
senses.exampleCN: 社会凝聚力取决于人们对同一套规则的信任。
senses.why: Bonds are not only emotional: they are made of expectations that others will behave predictably.
senses.whyCN: 纽带不只是情感：它们由「他人会按预期行事」的期待构成。

senses.title: A sociological concept
senses.definition: Durkheim's problem of what makes individual interests compatible with collective order
senses.definitionCN: 涂尔干提出的问题：个体利益如何与集体秩序相容
senses.example: Durkheim treated social cohesion as the effect of shared rituals and division of labour.
senses.exampleCN: 涂尔干把社会凝聚力视为共享仪式与分工的结果。
senses.why: The term names a classic question: how can many separate people remain one society at all?
senses.whyCN: 这个术语命名一个经典问题：许多分开的人究竟如何仍是一个社会？

senses.title: A policy goal
senses.definition: a stated aim of governments and foundations that fund inclusion, sport and public space
senses.definitionCN: 政府与基金会资助融合、体育与公共空间时所声明的目标
senses.example: The city put social cohesion in its five-year plan.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市把社会凝聚力写进了五年规划。
senses.why: Once measured, cohesion becomes something to be increased; the phrase turns from description into target.
senses.whyCN: 一旦可测量，凝聚力就变成可以被提高的东西；这个词组从描述变成目标。

senses.title: A measured index
senses.definition: a score built from trust surveys, volunteering rates or membership in associations
senses.definitionCN: 由信任调查、志愿活动率或社团参与度合成的分数
senses.example: The index shows social cohesion falling in the poorer districts.
senses.exampleCN: 该指数显示较贫困城区的社会凝聚力在下降。
senses.why: Policy needs numbers, so an abstract bond is converted into indicators that can be compared.
senses.whyCN: 政策需要数字，于是抽象的纽带被转换成可以比较的指标。

senses.title: The ethnic and religious dimension
senses.definition: the degree to which different ethnic or religious groups feel they belong to one society
senses.definitionCN: 不同族群或宗教群体感到自己属于同一个社会的程度
senses.example: Social cohesion weakened where one group was blamed for the shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 当短缺被归咎于某一个群体时，社会凝聚力就削弱了。
senses.why: Diversity tests the bond: the phrase often appears when groups must share institutions without sharing history.
senses.whyCN: 多样性会检验纽带：当群体必须共享制度却不共享历史时，这个词组常出现。

senses.title: Solidarity and the absence of conflict
senses.definition: the condition in which groups accept obligations to one another and disputes stay peaceful
senses.definitionCN: 各群体接受彼此义务、争端保持和平的状态
senses.example: The truce held because social cohesion was stronger than the quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 停战得以维持，因为社会凝聚力强于争吵。
senses.why: Cohesion can be read negatively, as what prevents a society from falling apart.
senses.whyCN: 凝聚力也可以反面地读，即防止社会散架的那种力量。

senses.title: Bridging across difference
senses.definition: the ties that connect separate groups rather than bind each group only to itself
